§ 10.01 TITLE OF CODE.
   All ordinances of a permanent and general nature, as revised, codified,
rearranged, renumbered and consolidated into component codes, titles, chapters
and sections, shall be known and designated as the “City of Sturgis Code,” for
which designation “code of ordinances” or “codified ordinances” may be
substituted. Code title, chapter and section headings do not constitute any
part of the law as contained in the code.
§ 10.02 RULES OF INTERPRETATION.
   (A)   Generally. Unless otherwise provided herein, or by law or implication
required, the same rules of construction, definition and application shall
govern the interpretation of this code as those governing the interpretation of
state law.
   (B)   Specific rules of interpretation. The construction of all ordinances
shall be by the following rules, unless that construction is plainly repugnant
to the intent of the legislative body or of the context of the same ordinance.
      (1)   Acts by assistants. When a statute, code provisions or ordinance
requires an act to be done which, by law, an agent or deputy as well may do as
the principal, that requisition shall be satisfied by the performance of the
act by an authorized agent or deputy.
      (2)   Gender; singular and plural; tenses. Words denoting the masculine
gender shall be deemed to include the feminine and neuter genders; words in the
singular shall include the plural, and words in the plural shall include the
singular; the use of a verb in the present tense shall include the future, if
applicable.
      (3)   General term. A general term following specific enumeration of
terms is not to be limited to the class enumerated unless expressly so limited.
General terms descriptive of an officer, act, proceeding or thing shall have
reference to a municipality concerned or affected.
Statutory reference:
   General terms descriptive of an officer, act, proceeding and the like, see
SDCL § 9-1-1
§ 10.03 CAPTIONS.
   Headings and captions used in this code other than the title, chapter and
section numbers are employed for reference purposes only and shall not be
deemed a part of the text of any section.
§ 10.04 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this code, the following definitions shall apply unless
the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   AGENT. A person acting on behalf of another with authority conferred, either
expressly or by implication.
   CITY. The City of Sturgis, Meade County, South Dakota.
   CITY COUNCIL. The City Council of the City of Sturgis. The words COMMON
COUNCIL and COUNCIL are synonymous with the words CITY COUNCIL.
   COMPUTATION OF TIME. The time in which any act provided by this code or
other ordinance is to be done is computed by excluding the first day and
including the last, unless the last is a holiday and then it also is excluded.
Fractions of a day are to be disregarded in computations which include more
than one day and involve no questions of priority.
   COUNTY. The County of Meade, South Dakota.
(SDCL § 9-1-1)
   DAY. A period of time between any midnight and the midnight following.
   DAYTIME, NIGHTTIME. DAYTIME is the period of time between sunrise and
sunset; NIGHTTIME is the period between sunset and sunrise.
   FEE. A sum of money charged by the city for the carrying on of a business,
profession or occupation.
   FISCAL YEAR. The fiscal year of the city begins on January 1 of each year.
   GOVERNING BODY. The board of trustees, the board of commissioners or the
common council of a municipality.
(SDCL § 9-1-1)
   HIGHWAYS or ROADS. Includes the whole of all public ways, roads, alleys,
courts and streets and sidewalks between the property lines forming the
exterior lateral boundaries thereof, and those parts of public squares and
places which form traveled parts of highways or roads.
   LICENSE. The permission granted for the carrying on of a business,
profession or occupation.
   LOT. Includes PARCEL or TRACT OF LAND.
(SDCL § 9-1-1)
   MONTH. A calendar month.
   MUNICIPALITY or MUNICIPAL CORPORATION. Any city or town that is organized
pursuant to SDCL Title 9.
(SDCL § 9-1-1)
   NUISANCE. Anything offensive to the sensibilities of reasonable persons, or
any act or activity creating a hazard which threatens the health and welfare of
inhabitants of the city, or any activity which by its perpetuation can
reasonably be said to have a detrimental effect on the property of a person or
persons within the community.
   OATH. Includes affirmation.
   OCCUPANT. As applied to a building or land, includes any person who occupies
the whole or any part of such building or land whether alone or with others.
   OFFENSE. Any act forbidden by any provision of this code, or the omission of
any act required by the provisions of this code.
   OFFICIAL TIME. Whenever certain hours are named herein they mean mountain
standard time or daylight saving time as may be in current use in the city.
   OPERATOR. The person who oversees any operation, business or profession.
   ORDINANCE. A permanent legislative act within the limits of its powers of
the governing body of a municipality.
(SDCL § 9-19-1)
   OWNER. The grantee in the last deed of conveyance of any lot or parcel of
land recorded in the office of the Register of Deeds of the county or counties
in which the municipality is located, or the heirs or successors to the
grantee.
(SDCL § 9-1-1)
   PERSON. Any public or private corporation, firm, partnership, association,
organization, government or any other group acting as a unit, as well as a
natural person.
   PERSONAL PROPERTY. Includes every description of money, goods, chattels,
effects, evidence of rights in action and all written instruments by which any
pecuniary obligation, right or title to property is created, acknowledged,
transferred, increased, defeated, discharged or diminished and every right or
interest therein.
   PRECEDING, FOLLOWING. Next before and next after, respectively.
   PROCESS. Includes a writ or summons issued during judicial proceedings.
   PROPERTY. Includes real and personal property.
   PUBLISH. Publication in an official newspaper of the municipality as
designated by the governing body pursuant to SDCL § 9-12-6.
(SDCL § 9-1-1)
   REAL PROPERTY. Includes lands, tenements and hereditaments.
   RETAILER. Unless otherwise specifically defined, is understood to relate to
the sale of goods, merchandise, articles or things direct to the consumer.
   RIGHT-OF-WAY. The privilege of the immediate use of the roadway or other
property.
   RESOLUTION. Any determination, decision or direction of the governing body
of a municipality of a temporary or special character for the purpose of
initiating effecting or carrying out its administrative duties and functions.
(SDCL § 9-19-1)
   SIGNATURE or SUBSCRIPTION BY MARK. Includes a mark when the signer or
subscriber cannot write, such signer’s or subscriber’s name being written near
the mark by a witness who signs his or her own name near the signer’s or
subscriber’s name.
   STATE. The State of South Dakota.
   STREET. Includes alleys, lanes, courts, boulevards, public ways, public
squares, public places and sidewalks.
   SDCL. South Dakota Codified Laws.
   TENANT or OCCUPANT. As applied to a building or land, includes any person
holding a written or an oral lease of or who occupies the whole or a part of
such building or land, either alone or with others.
   WEEK. A week consists of seven consecutive days.
   WHOLESALER. Unless otherwise specifically defined, relates to the sale of
goods, merchandise, articles or things to persons who buy for the purpose of
resale.
   WRITTEN, IN WRITING. May include printing and any other mode of representing
words and letters, but when the written signature of any person is required by
law to any official or public writing or bond, it is the handwriting of such
person, or if such person is unable to write, by the person’s proper mark.
   YEAR. A calendar year.
(Prior Code, § 1.01.05) (Ord. 2024-07, passed 10-3-2024)
§ 10.05 SEVERABILITY.
   If any provision of this code as now or later amended or its application to
any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect
other provisions that can be given effect without the invalid provision or
application.
§ 10.06 REFERENCE TO OTHER SECTIONS.
   Whenever in one section reference is made to another section hereof, that
reference shall extend and apply to the section referred to as subsequently
amended, revised, recodified or renumbered unless the subject matter is changed
or materially altered by the amendment or revision.
§ 10.07 REFERENCE TO OFFICES.
   Reference to a public office or officer shall be deemed to apply to any
office, officer or employee of this local government exercising the powers,
duties or functions contemplated in the provision, irrespective of any transfer
of functions or change in the official title of the functionary.
§ 10.08 ERRORS AND OMISSIONS.
   If a manifest error is discovered, consisting of the misspelling of any
words; the omission of any word or words necessary to express the intention of
the provisions affected; the use of a word or words to which no meaning can be
attached; or the use of a word or words when another word or words was clearly
intended to express the intent, the spelling shall be corrected and the word or
words supplied, omitted or substituted as will conform with the manifest
intention, and the provisions shall have the same effect as though the correct
words were contained in the text as originally published. No alteration shall
be made or permitted if any question exists regarding the nature or extent of
the error.
§ 10.09 POWERS TO ENACT, AMEND OR REPEAL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS; GENERALLY.
   Every municipality may enact, make, amend, revise or repeal all such
ordinances, resolutions and regulations as may be proper and necessary to carry
into effect the powers granted thereto.
§ 10.10 ORDINANCES REPEALED.
   This code, from and after its effective date, shall contain all of the
provisions of a general nature pertaining to the subjects herein enumerated and
embraced. All prior ordinances pertaining to the subjects treated by this code
shall be deemed repealed from and after the effective date of this code.
§ 10.11 ORDINANCES UNAFFECTED.
   All ordinances of a temporary or special nature and all other ordinances
pertaining to subjects not embraced in this code shall remain in full force and
effect unless herein repealed expressly or by necessary implication.
§ 10.12 REPEAL OR MODIFICATION OF AN ORDINANCE.
   (A)   No suit, proceedings, right, fine, forfeiture or penalty instituted,
created, given, secured or accrued under any ordinance previous to its repeal
shall in any way be affected, released or discharged, but may be prosecuted,
enjoined and recovered as fully as if the ordinance had continued in force
unless it is otherwise expressly provided.
   (B)   When any ordinance repealing a former ordinance, clause or provision
shall be itself repealed, the repeal shall not be construed to revive the
former ordinance, clause or provision, unless it is expressly provided.
§ 10.13 ORDINANCES WHICH AMEND OR SUPPLEMENT CODE.
   (A)   If the legislative body shall desire to amend any existing chapter or
section of this code, the chapter or section shall be specifically repealed and
a new chapter or section, containing the desired amendment, substituted in its
place.
   (B)   Any ordinance which is proposed to add to the existing code a new
chapter or section shall indicate, with reference to the arrangement of this
code, the proper number of the chapter or section. In addition to this
indication as may appear in the text of the proposed ordinance, a caption or
title shall be shown in concise form above the ordinance.
§ 10.14 PRESERVATION OF PENALTIES, OFFENSES, RIGHTS AND LIABILITIES.
   All offenses committed under laws in force prior to the effective date of
this code shall be prosecuted and remain punishable as provided by those laws.
This code does not affect any rights or liabilities accrued, penalties incurred
or proceedings begun prior to the effective date of this code. The liabilities,
proceedings and rights are continued; punishments, penalties or forfeitures
shall be enforced and imposed as if this code had not been enacted. In
particular, any agreement granting permission to utilize highway rights-of-way,
contracts entered into or franchises granted, the acceptance, establishment or
vacation of any highway, and the election of corporate officers shall remain
valid in all respects, as if this code had not been enacted.
§ 10.99 GENERAL PENALTY.
   (A)   Violation of provisions. Any person violating any of the provisions of
this code or failing to comply with any of the provisions hereof may, upon
conviction thereof, be punished by a fine as shall be set forth in the city’s
annual fee resolution or by imprisonment for a period not exceeding 30 days or
by both such fine and imprisonment. Each violation of the provisions of this
code constitutes a separate offense.
   (B)   Application of provisions.
      (1)   The penalty provided in this chapter applies to every section of
this code the same as though it were a part of each separate section. Any
person convicted of a violation if any section of this code where any duty is
prescribed or obligation imposed, or where any action which is of a continuing
nature is forbidden or is declared to be unlawful, is guilty of a Class 2
misdemeanor. A separate offense is committed upon each day such duty or
obligation remains unperformed or such act continues, unless otherwise
specifically provided in this code.
      (2)   In all cases where the same offense is punishable or is created by
different clauses or sections of this code, the prosecuting officer may elect
under which to proceed, but not more than one recovery may be had against the
same person for the same offense; provided, that the revocation of a license or
permit is not a recovery or penalty to bar any other penalty being enforced.
      (3)   Whenever the doing of any act or the omission to do any act
constitutes a breach of any section or provision of this code and there is no
fine or penalty specifically declared for such breach, the provisions of this
chapter apply.
   (C)   Liability of officers. No provision of this code designating the
duties of any officer or employee makes any such officer or employee liable for
any fine or penalty provided for a failure to perform such duty, unless the
City Council’s intent to impose such fine or penalty on such officer or
employee is specifically and clearly expressed in the section creating the
duty.
(Prior Code, § 1.01.07) (Ord. 2024-07, passed 10-3-2024)
Statutory reference:
   Related provisions, see SDCL §§ 9-19-3 and 22-6-2(2)

§ 30.01 ALDERMANIC FORM OF GOVERNMENT.
   The city is governed under the aldermanic form of government as provided by
the state law, with the governing body being the City Council consisting of a
Mayor and two aldermen from each of the four wards of the city. The conduct of
city government must conform to state law and this code. Whenever any provision
of this code conflicts with state law, the applicable provision of state law
supersedes this code. Unless lodged elsewhere, all the corporate and political
powers of the city are vested in the City Council.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.01)
§ 30.02 MAYOR.
   (A)   The Mayor is the chief executive officer of the city and presides over
the meetings of the City Council. The voters of the city elect the Mayor at
large at the general municipal election for a term of three years.
    (B)   Any vacancy in the office of Mayor must be filled as provided by
state law and this code. The Mayor performs such duties and exercise such
powers as provided by state law and this code.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.02)
§ 30.03 CITY COUNCIL.
   (A)   The City Council is the general legislative body of the city. The City
Council consists of two aldermen elected by the voters of each of the four
election wards of the city and serve a regular term of three years; provided,
that the terms of the aldermen from each ward are staggered so that the regular
terms of the aldermen of a ward do not expire in the same year.
   (B)   Any vacancy in the office of alderman must be filled as provided by
state law and this code. The City Council performs such duties and exercises
such powers as provided by state law and this code.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.03)
§ 30.04 CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS.
   (A)   Regular meetings. The regular meetings of the City Council are held on
the first and third Mondays of each month of the year at 6:30 p.m. unless
otherwise determined by the City Council, such an hour as the City Council may
fix from time to time. Regular meetings are held in the City Hall unless
another site is specified. Any regular meeting falling on a legal holiday must
be held on the Tuesday immediately following such a Monday holiday.
   (B)   Special meetings. Special City Council meetings may be called by the
Mayor or, in the Mayor’s absence, by the Council President and scheduled as
soon as reasonably possible. Special meetings may also be called by the Finance
Officer at the written request of three members of the City Council and
scheduled as soon as reasonably as possible. Special meetings of the Council
encompass only such matters as are mentioned in the notice for the special
meeting.
      (1)   Notice of special meetings must include a proposed agenda with the
date, time and location of the meeting. The notice must be posted as provided
in state law at least 24 hours prior to the meeting or as far in advance as the
circumstances allow.
      (2)   Notice of special meetings must be provided, as authorized by state
law, to each Council member and to local news outlets requesting notice.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.04)
§ 30.05 COUNCIL PROCEDURES.
   Robert’s Rules of Order: The 11th edition is the standard by which all
regular meetings of the Council are governed. Any suspension of the procedure
of a Council meeting, except as provided by city ordinance, must be as provided
for in those Rules.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.05)
§ 30.06 MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS.
   (A)   Election wards.
      (1)   The city is hereby divided into four wards, each of which consists
of a voting precinct.
         (a)   The First Ward is that portion of the city located within the
following boundary: Beginning at the intersection of the centerlines of Glencoe
Drive and State Highway 34, then following the city boundary south and west to
the extension of Sherman Street right-of-way, then continuing west along
Sherman Street to its intersection with the DM&E railroad track, then
continuing northwesterly along the railroad track to its intersection with
Interstate 90, then continuing southwesterly along Interstate 90 to the
southern city limits, then westerly along the south city limits to the western
boundary of city limits, then northerly along the western city limits to the
northern boundary of city limits, then following the northern boundary of city
limits east to the intersection of the centerlines of Glencoe Drive and State
Highway 34; excluding all unincorporated areas within the bounded area. This
area must also include that portion of the noncontiguous city boundary to
include the city owned municipal airport property.
         (b)   The Second Ward is that portion of the city located within the
following boundary: Beginning at the intersection of the centerlines of
Junction Avenue and Sherman Street, then continuing westerly along Sherman
Street to its intersection with the DM&E railroad track, then continuing
northwesterly along the railroad track to its intersection with Interstate 90,
then continuing southwesterly along the west city limits lying north of
Interstate 90, then continuing southwesterly along the north side of Interstate
90 to its intersection with Vanocker Canyon Road, then continuing north along
Vanocker Canyon Road to its intersection with Junction Avenue, then continuing
northerly along Junction Avenue back to its intersection with Sherman Street.
         (c)   The Third Ward is that portion of the city located within the
following boundary: Beginning at the intersection of the centerlines of
Junction Avenue and Sherman Street, then continuing southerly along Junction
Avenue to its intersection with Vanocker Canyon Road, then continuing southerly
along Vanocker Canyon Road to its intersection with 1st Avenue, then continuing
westerly along 1st Avenue to its intersection with Vanocker Drive, then
continuing southerly along Vanocker Drive to its intersection with Pine View
Drive, then continuing westerly along Pine View Drive to its intersection with
the western city limits, then following city limits south and east to its
intersection with Vanocker Canyon Road, then continuing northerly along
Vanocker Canyon Road to its intersection with the DM&E railroad track, then
northerly along the eastern city limits back to its intersection with the
extension of Sherman Street right-of-way, then continuing westerly along
Sherman Street back to its intersection with Junction Avenue.
         (d)   The Fourth Ward is that portion of the city located within the
following boundary: Beginning at the intersection of the centerlines of
Vanocker Canyon Road and Interstate 90, then continuing south along Vanocker
Canyon Road to its intersection with 1st Avenue, then continuing westerly along
1st Avenue to its intersection with Vanocker Drive, then continuing southerly
along Vanocker Drive to its intersection with Pine View Drive, then continuing
westerly along Pine View Drive to the western boundary of city limits, then
following the western city boundary north to its intersection with Interstate
90, then southwesterly along Interstate 90 back to its intersection with
Vanocker Canyon Road.
      (2)   This section becomes effective upon the passage and publication
thereof, the same being necessary for the support of the municipal government
and its existing public institutions.
   (B)   Polling hours. The election polls for the annual election of officers
and any special municipal election must be open continuously from 7:00 a.m.
until 7:00 p.m.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.06) (Ord. 2001-29, passed 2-1-2002; Ord. 2011-08, passed
12-27-2011; Ord. 2021-12, passed 1-28-2022)
§ 30.07 BOARDS AND COMMISSIONS APPOINTED BY THE MAYOR.
   The Mayor, with the advice and approval of the Common Council, must make
appointments to Council subcommittees. The Mayor may make appointments to all
other city boards and commissions, except as otherwise provided by state law in
the case of Municipal Utility Board members, or this code.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.07) (Ord. 2023-03, passed 5-2-2023)
§ 30.08 APPOINTMENT OF COUNCIL MEMBERS TO BOARDS AND COMMITTEES.
   (A)   Following the election of officers at the first meeting of the Council
each May, each Council member must have an opportunity to make their request,
identifying the order of importance, for the member to be appointed to any of
the “outside” boards or commissions listed in this section. Following that
meeting, the Mayor, with the advice and approval of the Common Council, may
make Council member appointments for a one-year term to each board or
commission listed below:
      (1)   Planning and Zoning Commission;
      (2)   Library Board;
      (3)   City Chamber of Commerce Board;
      (4)   Parks Board, including Forestry Board responsibilities;
      (5)   Transportation Board;
      (6)   City Motorcycle Museum Board;
      (7)   City Rally Charities;
      (8)   County Senior Citizens Center Board;
      (9)   City Economic Development Corporation;
      (10)   Legal and Finance Council subcommittee (comprised of Mayor,
Council President, Council Vice President and one other Council member);
      (11)   Rally and Events Council subcommittee; and
      (12)   Infrastructure Advisory Council subcommittee.
   (B)   For other ad hoc committees, each Council member must have an
opportunity to make his or her recommendation for the Council members to be
appointed to that committee. Thereafter, the Mayor, with the advice and
approval of the Common Council, may make appointments to such an ad hoc
committee or committees.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.08) (Ord. 2023-03, passed 5-2-2023)
§ 30.09 ELECTION OF PRESIDENT AND VICE PRESIDENT.
   At the first meeting of the Council in May of each year, and after the
qualification of the newly elected Council Members, the Council must elect from
among its own members a President and Vice President of the Council, whose
duties are prescribed by the laws of the state. Nominations for the office of
Council President must be made by members of the Council and when nominations
close then ballots must be cast for that office. If more than two candidates
are nominated, then the vote must be by public vote, to be reviewed and counted
by the Finance Officer and an assistant. After the votes are tabulated, the
Finance Officer must report the ballot tabulation and state the name of the
person elected. Following that election, nominations for the office of Council
Vice President must be made by members of the Council and when nominations
close then voting for that office must take place in the same manner as for
Council President.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.09)
§ 30.10 VACANCIES ON THE COMMON COUNCIL OR IN THE OFFICE OF MAYOR.
   (A)   If a vacancy exists on the Common Council, the remaining members may
appoint a replacement to serve until the next annual municipal election, or by
special election called for that purpose as provided in SDCL § 9-13-14 and this
chapter. The appointee must be a person from the same ward of the municipality.
When electing a person to fill the remainder of the unexpired term at an annual
municipal election, the vacancy must have occurred prior to the publication
required by SDCL § 9-13-6.
   (B)   If there is a vacancy from any cause in the office of the Mayor, the
vacancy may be filled by appointment by a majority vote of the aldermen, as
soon as practicable after the vacancy occurs, to serve until the office is
filled by election for the unexpired term at the next annual municipal election
or by special election called for that purpose, as provided in SDCL § 9-13-14
and this chapter. Until the vacancy is filled or, during the time of temporary
absence or disability of the Mayor, the powers and duties of the Mayor are
executed by the President or Vice President of the Council, as provided in SDCL
§ 9-8-7. When electing a person to fill the remainder of the unexpired term at
an annual municipal election, the vacancy must have occurred prior to the
publication required by SDCL § 9-13-6. No special election may be held less
than 90 days before the annual municipal election.
   (C)   If a vacancy is to be filled by special election, the Finance Officer
must publish a notice in the official newspaper of the municipality stating
that a vacancy exists, that the vacancy will be filled by special election, the
date of the election and the time and place where nominating petitions may be
filed for the office. The notice must be published once each week for two
consecutive weeks beginning at least 60 days before the date of the special
election.
   (D)   Nominating petitions for the vacancy must be prepared and filed as
provided in SDCL § 9-13-7, may not be circulated more than 60 days before the
date of the special election, and must be filed at least 30 days before the
date of the special election. The number of signatures required for a
nominating petition must be calculated as provided in SDCL § 9-13-9. If a
nominating petition is filed before the second Tuesday in January, the prior
year’s calculation of registered voters must be used to determine the number of
needed signatures. The Finance Officer must publish a notice of the special
election as provided in SDCL §§ 9-13-13 and 9-13-14 and must publish a copy of
the official ballot in the official city newspaper the week before the
election.
(Prior Code, § 7.01.10) (Ord. 2024-03, passed - -)

**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 31.01 APPOINTMENT PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Appointive officers and positions. The following named offices and
positions in the city are appointed positions, pursuant to state law and this
code: City Administrator; Finance Officer; Director of Public Works; Chief of
Police; Director of EMS; Director of Community Center; Director of Municipal
Liquor Store; Director of Administrative Services and Human Resources; Director
of Rally and Events; Director of Sponsorship Development; City Attorney;
Director of Planning and Permitting; City Librarian; and Director of
Communications and Outreach.
   (B)   Qualifications and appointments.
      (1)   The qualifying requirements for all appointive officers of the city
must be in accordance with the qualification requirements for appointment to
office as established by state law, or as established by this code.
      (2)   The Mayor appoints each officer with the approval of the City
Council. Appointed officers serve at the pleasure of the Mayor, and their
appointment may be terminated by the Mayor, with or without cause, at any time,
pursuant to SDCL § 9-14-13. The Mayor must report the reasons for such
termination to the City Council at the next regular meeting. Such officers must
be appointed or reappointed with each new Mayoral term with Council approval.
   (C)   Oath and undertaking required. Each appointed officer, before entering
upon the discharge of his or her duties, must take and subscribe an oath or
affirmation of office in the form required by the Constitution of the State.
Each appointed officer must furnish an undertaking to the city in the sum as
shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution except for the Finance
Officer and City Administrator who must furnish an undertaking to the city in
the amount as shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution. Said bond
must be conditioned for the faithful performance of the duties of their
respective officers and to account for, pay over and deliver all money coming
into their hands by virtue of the office, according to law. Bonds for deputies
must be determined by the appointing officer.
   (D)   Salaries and reimbursements.
      (1)   Generally. The annual salaries of all appointive officers and
employees of the city are as prescribed from time to time by the City Council.
      (2)   Reimbursement for expenses. No officer or employee of the city is
entitled to reimbursement for personal expenses incurred in the discharge of
his or her official duties except as approved by the City Council; requests for
reimbursement must conform to such procedures as adopted by the City Council.
   (E)   General duties. The duties of the various appointive officers of the
city are such as are ordinarily undertaken by such officers and as provided by
state law, this code and the job description, if any, applicable to such
office. Such officers must also perform such further duties as may be assigned
to them by the Mayor or the City Council if the City Council has been
authorized to prescribe such duties.
(Prior Code, § 7.02.01)
§ 31.02 GENERAL EXECUTIVE CHAIN OF COMMAND.
   (A)   The official business and administration of the city is executed and
implemented through a chain of command, with the Mayor as the chief executive
officer of the city and responsible for executing and implementing the
legislative decisions and policies established by the City Council through the
various department heads and departments of the city. The department heads are
directly accountable to the Mayor. No individual alderman, or group of
aldermen, has the authority to direct the actions of a department head or any
subordinate employee within the city. Nothing contained in this code is
intended to impair the ability of the Mayor or any alderman to consult with any
department head or subordinate employee regarding the affairs of the city, nor
does anything contained herein impair the ability of the City Council to call
any employee to testify before the City Council in executive session in respect
to matters properly addressable in executive session as provided by law.
   (B)   Annually during the budget process, the Mayor, with the approval of
the City Council, must establish by resolution a more precise organizational
chart implementing the chain of command described in this chapter, and revise
such organizational chart from time to time.
(Prior Code, § 7.02.02)
§ 31.03 GENERAL APPEAL PROCEDURES.
   (A)   Unless otherwise provided, any person aggrieved by a decision or other
act of an employee or officer of the city, excluding any employment disputes
and allegations of violation of law resulting in prosecution, has the right to
appeal such act or decision to the City Council.
   (B)   An appeal must be started by filing a written notice of appeal with
the Finance Office within ten business days of the date of the action which is
subject to appeal. The Finance Officer must place the matter for hearing and
consideration by the City Council, excluding personnel matters which must be
addressed in executive session, at the next regularly scheduled meeting
occurring at least five business days after the notice of appeal is received.
The Finance Officer must notify the aggrieved person and city personnel of the
time and place at which the City Council will decide the appeal.
   (C)   Notice by certified mail to the appellant at the address shown on the
notice of appeal provides good and sufficient notice.
   (D)   The City Council may, in its discretion, continue an appeal hearing to
another time, provided that the continuance is for a reasonable length of time.
Any person aggrieved by the City Council’s decision may appeal such decision as
allowed by state law.
(Prior Code, § 7.02.03)
**** CITY ADMINISTRATOR ****
§ 31.15 CITY ADMINISTRATOR APPOINTMENT.
   The Mayor may appoint a City Administrator with the approval of the City
Council. The City Administrator serves at the pleasure of the Mayor and may be
terminated by the Mayor, with or without cause, at any time pursuant to SDCL §
9-14-13. The Mayor must report the reasons for such termination to the City
Council at the next regular meeting. The City Administrator must be appointed
or reappointed with each new Mayoral term with Council approval.
(Prior Code, § 7.03.01) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
§ 31.16 CITY ADMINISTRATOR QUALIFICATIONS.
   The City Administrator must be appointed solely based on executive and
administrative qualifications. The City Administrator need not be a resident of
the city or state at the time of appointment but must reside in the city while
in office in conjunction with his or her employment agreement.
(Prior Code, § 7.03.02) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
§ 31.17 POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR.
   The City Administrator is the chief administrative officer of the city,
responsible to the Mayor for the administration of all city affairs placed in
the City Administrator’s charge by this code and city resolutions. The City
Administrator’s duties include:
   (A)   Ensuring that all provisions of this code and all acts of the City
Council subject to enforcement are faithfully executed by the City
Administrator or employees subject to the City Administrator’s direction and
supervision;
   (B)   Overseeing and directing the administration of all departments,
offices and agencies of the city, except as otherwise provided by state law or
this code;
   (C)   Making recommendations to the City Council concerning city affairs;
   (D)   Preparing and submitting to the City Council an annual budget not
later than September 1 of each year;
   (E)   Ensuring all terms and conditions in any contract or franchise to
which the city is a party are faithfully kept and performed;
   (F)   Directing the hiring, reassignment and promotion of all city
employees;
   (G)   When necessary, suspending or removing any city employee except as
otherwise provided by state law, this code or personnel policies adopted by the
City Council;
   (H)   Serving as the liaison between the Mayor, the City Council and city
staff;
   (I)   Attending all meetings of the City Council, except as excused by the
Mayor;
   (J)   Keeping the City Council advised as to future city needs;
   (K)   Providing staff support services for the Mayor and City Council
members;
   (L)   Submitting updates and reports to the City Council as requested;
   (M)   Delegating authority with specific guidelines as considered
appropriate; and
    (N)   Performing such other duties as are required by the City
Administrator job description, by resolution or as may be required from time to
time by the Mayor.
(Prior Code, § 7.03.03) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
§ 31.18 ACTING CITY ADMINISTRATOR AND ALTERNATIVE APPOINTMENT.
   In the absence of a City Administrator, the Mayor, with the approval of the
City Council, may appoint a designee or designees to exercise the powers and
perform the duties of the City Administrator during the Administrator’s
temporary absence or disability.
(Prior Code, § 7.03.04) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
§ 31.19 AUTHORITY TO APPROVE EXPENDITURES AND ENTER INTO CONTRACTS.
   (A)   The Mayor, or City Administrator with approval of the City Council,
has the authority to sign and approve any expenditures, contracts or agreements
(unless related to sponsorship of the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally) on behalf of
the city that have appropriations. Such expenditures, contracts or agreements
that exceed the amount set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution must be
countersigned by either the Finance Officer, City Attorney, Director of
Administrative Services or Public Works Director. No claim may be paid until
approved by the City Council, except as may be otherwise provided by this code
or city resolution.
   (B)   The Mayor, or City Administrator with approval of the City Council,
has the authority to sign sponsorship agreements and licensing agreements.
(Prior Code, § 7.03.05) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)

**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 32.01 ORGANIZATION.
   The operations of the city are organized into departments as provided in
this code. Unless otherwise provided by state law or this code, the Mayor, with
the approval of the City Council, may assign duties to each department. Each
department, as appropriate, may be further organized into divisions consisting
of the areas of responsibility assigned to the department (example: the Public
Works Department may consist of engineering/inspection, streets and sanitation,
water, wastewater and airport, each as a division within the Public Works
Department).
(Prior Code, § 7.04.01) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
§ 32.02 DEPARTMENT HEADS.
   (A)   (1)   Each department must have an executive who is an appointed
officer of the city and who is known as the department head or department
director of each respective department. If so appointed, one individual may
serve as the director of more than one department.
      (2)   The department head is the senior executive officer of the
department, and exercises the personnel, administrative and coordinating
authority for the department and the divisions therein, and is responsible,
further subordinate delegation of authority notwithstanding, for the
management, administration and execution of the city operations within the
department, subject to the executive and administrative authority of the Mayor
and the City Council as provided by state law and this code.
      (3)   (a)   A department head may delegate to subordinate personnel
within the department the duties and responsibilities of the department head
and the corresponding authority to perform such duties and responsibilities.
         (b)   The term DEPARTMENT includes all the divisions within the
department. The department head is responsible for the actions of any
subordinate within the department, decisions of a subordinate are considered
the action of the department head, notwithstanding that subordinate employees
may be assigned specific duties and responsibilities within this code.
Likewise, each manager or superintendent within any division of a department is
responsible for the official actions of subordinates and the official action of
the subordinate is considered the actions of the superior authority.
   (B)   Each department head must:
      (1)   Be responsible for administration management and operation of the
department;
      (2)   Assign the positions and duties of all full-time and part-time
personnel of the department;
      (3)   Make necessary and proper rules for the operational governance of
the department;
      (4)   Be responsible for the conduct and discipline of the personnel of
the department;
      (5)   Be responsible for the care, maintenance and condition of the
property of the city assigned to the department; and
      (6)   Have command of all employees assigned to the department. Have such
further duties as may be assigned to them by the Mayor or the City Council if
the City Council has been authorized to prescribe such duties.
(Prior Code, § 7.04.01) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
**** DEPARTMENTS, COUNCILS AND BOARDS ****
§ 32.15 FINANCE OFFICE.
   (A)   Department established. The Department of the Finance Office is hereby
established.
   (B)   Finance Officer.
      (1)   The Finance Officer is the department head of the Finance
Department and the chief financial officer of the city. The Finance Officer
performs all the duties of a City Auditor and City Treasurer, as such duties
are provided for by state law and this code. Whenever reference is made in
state law, this code or other official document to the term MUNICIPAL AUDITOR,
MUNICIPAL TREASURER MUNICIPAL CLERK or the equivalent thereof, the term has the
same meaning as Finance Officer.
      (2)   The Finance Officer must be bonded in the same amount as is
required by law for a city treasurer.
      (3)   The Finance Officer must keep regular books of account in which
showing all indebtedness of the city, and which at all times show the financial
condition of the city, the amount of bonds, warrants, certificates or other
evidences of indebtedness issued by the city, and the amounts of all bonds,
warrants, certificates or other evidences of indebtedness which have been
redeemed and the amount of each outstanding.
(Prior Code, § 7.04.02) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)

§ 32.17 PUBLIC SAFETY DEPARTMENTS.
   (A)   City Police Department.
      (1)   Chief of Police. The Chief of Police is the department head of the
Police Department and performs such duties as may be provided by state law and
this code.
      (2)   Special powers and duties. The Chief of Police, subject to the
administrative supervision of the Mayor, or the committee appointed by Mayor
with the approval of the City Council for such purpose, is responsible for:
         (a)   The enforcement of state and local laws and police ordinances
within the city;
         (b)   The supervision of the Communications Division;
         (c)   The supervision of the city’s code enforcement personnel; and
         (d)   Such other duties which may be provided in the position job
description.
      (3)   Operational powers in absence of Chief. If the Chief of Police is
absent or incapacitated, and in the event of the occurrence of a law
enforcement emergency posing a threat to public safety and order, the on-scene
police officer in command has the same on-scene operational powers as the Chief
of Police.
      (4)   Require aid. In the execution of the duties of any police officer
in arresting any person accused or suspected of any crime or any suppression of
any riot or unlawful assembly, or in the prevention of any offense against the
city or state, said officer has the power, when necessary, to require the aid
of any citizen; and it is unlawful for any person to refuse or willfully
neglect to obey the summons of any police officer in such cases.
   (B)   Department of Emergency Medical Services (EMS).
      (1)   Director of EMS. The Director of EMS is the department head of the
EMS Department and performs all such duties as provided by state law and this
code.
      (2)   Special powers and duties. The Director of EMS, subject to the
administrative supervision of the Mayor, or the committee appointed by Mayor
with the approval of the City Council for such purpose, is responsible for and
may have such other duties which may be provided in the position job
description.
(Prior Code, § 7.04.04) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012) Penalty, see §

of any city ordinance are not changed.

§ 32.27 PLANNING COMMISSION.
   (A)   Official name. That the official name of the Planning Commission
created hereunder is the “Sturgis City Planning and Zoning Commission”
hereafter referred to as “Commission.”
(Prior Code, § 7.08.01)
   (B)   Establishment and composition. The City Planning and Zoning Commission
consists of seven members appointed by the Mayor, with the approval of the
Common Council, and to hold office as set forth by state law. The term of
appointment for each Commissioner is three years, and each Commissioner may
serve two consecutive full terms. The membership must choose one of its members
as Chairperson and in addition one member of the City Council must sit as an ex
officio member of the Commission.
(Prior Code, § 7.08.02)
   (C)   Commission budget and member qualifications.
      (1)   The annual budget ordinance must include funds necessary for the
conduct of the activities of the Commission.
      (2)   All Commissioners must reside within the city and be registered
voters, or own property within the city, at the time of their appointment and
for the duration of their term. Individuals with expertise in civil
engineering, architecture, real estate, land development, public or private
utilities, law, public education, government, community services, business,
industry, environmental matters, family issues or any other specialty that will
provide a broad, qualified and balanced representation of the community are
encouraged to apply. Members of the Planning Commission must be qualified by
knowledge or experience to act in matters pertaining to the development and
administration of a comprehensive plan of development for the city.
      (3)   All Commissioners are entitled to receive free membership to the
City Community Center or a half-price family membership to the City Community
Center. In addition, each Commissioner and a guest must be invited to the
annual city Christmas party.
(Prior Code, § 7.08.03)
   (D)   Powers and duties.
      (1)   The City Planning and Zoning Commission must execute its functions
in accordance with SDCL Chapter 11-6 and has all the powers, duties and
responsibilities as set forth in said statutes. In addition to the duties under
state law and other applicable duties established in Title XV, the Commission’s
duties include review of design standards and appeals of design denials within
the Downtown Overlay District, review and recommendations to the Common Council
of plats, variances and uses on review. The Commission must conduct their
meetings using Robert’s Rules of Orders.
      (2)   The Commission members do not act as the Board of Adjustment,
because the City Council holds that authority.
(Prior Code, § 7.08.04)
(Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012; Ord. 2019-05, passed 7-2-2019; Ord. 2023-03,
passed 5-2-2023)
§ 32.28 ARTS COUNCIL.
   (A)   Scope and purpose. The purpose of this section is to recognize the
City Area Arts Council and designate it as the organization to assist the city
in promoting and encouraging public programs to further the development and
awareness of and interest in the arts.
(Prior Code, § 22.01.01)
   (B)   Benefits to citizens. The artists and artistic institutions of the
city contribute to and provide cultural, educational, entertainment and
recreational benefits available to and used by the citizens of the city.
(Prior Code, § 22.02.01)
   (C)   City Area Arts Council essential to public welfare. The establishment
of the City Area Arts Council has promoted and encouraged public programs to
further the development and public awareness of and interest in the arts which
is essential to the public welfare.
(Prior Code, § 22.02.02)
   (D)   Designation of City Area Arts Council. The City Council does hereby
designate the Area Arts Council as the organization to assist the city in
promoting and encouraging public programs to further the development and
awareness of and interest in the arts and to act in an advisory capacity to the
city in connection with the artistic and cultural development of the city.
(Prior Code, § 22.02.03)
   (E)   Authority of City Area Arts Council. The Area Arts Council is hereby
authorized to initiate, sponsor and conduct public programs to further the
development and awareness of, and interest in, the arts.
(Prior Code, § 22.02.04)
   (F)   Additional advice and assistance upon request. The Area Arts Council
is to advise and assist the city in connection with such other artistic
activities as may be referred to it by the city.
(Prior Code, § 22.02.05)
(Ord. 2006-12, passed 5-27-2006)
§ 32.29 ARTS COUNCIL PUBLIC ART COMMITTEE.
   (A)   Establishment.
      (1)   The City Council has determined that it is in the best interests of
the city to establish the Area Arts Council Public Art Committee. The Public
Art Committee acting through the Area Arts Council shall administer the
provisions of this section relating to the selection, display, maintenance,
repair, liability and ownership of public works of art.
      (2)   The Area Arts Council Public Art Committee is a volunteer committee
of the Area Arts Council, and said Committee shall operate in an advisory
capacity to the City Council on art in public places, and its members shall be
appointed by the Area Arts Council President and Board of Directors, subject to
the approval of the Mayor.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.01)
   (B)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      ART IN PUBLIC PLACES. Any visual work of art displayed for three months
or more in an open city owned area, public right-of-way or any exterior or
interior designated as a city owned public area, and any visual work of art on
non-city property if it is installed, financed or maintained, either wholly or
in part, with city funds or grants procured by the city, but not including
museums, art galleries, school class work or any other works submitted to the
Council for display in a city owned facility.
      WORK OF ART. Includes, but is not limited to, sculpture, monument, mural,
fresco, relief, painting, photography, fountain, banner, mosaic, ceramic,
weaving, carving and stained glass. WORK OF ART would normally not include
landscaping, paving, architectural ornamentation or signs.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.02)
   (C)   Administration. The Area Arts Council shall provide administrative
support and assistance to the Public Art Committee as necessary to accomplish
the purposes of this section. The Committee shall submit to the City Council,
not later than March of each year, a report of its activities of the prior
year. The Area Arts Council, in conjunction with the Public Art Committee,
shall prepare a maintenance plan for all art in public places and will include
the costs associated therewith as part of the Area Arts Council’s budget
request to the City Council.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.03)
   (D)   Committee to adopt guidelines. The Area Arts Council Public Art
Committee shall adopt guidelines as follows:
      (1)   To identify suitable art works for public display;
      (2)   To facilitate the preservation of art works for public display;
      (3)   To prescribe a method or methods and procedures for selection of
art works for public display; and
      (4)   To set forth any other matter appropriate to the administration of
this section.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.04)
   (E)   Ownership. Ownership, title and copyright of works of art in public
places acquired by the procedures identified by the Area Arts Council pursuant
to this section shall be clearly identified and contracted between the Area
Arts Council and the artist or donor and approved and held by the city.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.05)
   (F)   Selection, removal and/or alterations. Any proposed art in public
places shall be submitted to the Public Art Committee for its recommendation
and approved by the City Council. No art in public places shall be removed,
altered or changed without the prior review and recommendation of the Committee
and approval by the City Council.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.06)
   (G)   Exemptions. The following are exempt from the provisions of this
section:
      (1)   All works of art in the collections or on display under the
auspices of the Area Arts Council sponsored gallery and the Public Library; and
      (2)   All works of art on display in private city offices or other areas
of city owned facilities that are not generally frequented by the public.
(Prior Code, § 22.03.07)
(Ord. 2006-12, passed 5-27-2006)
§ 32.30 EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM.
   (A)   Purpose. The purpose of this section is to allow for the establishment
of an Emergency Response Team to assist the Mayor in performing his duties
consistent with the power granted the Mayor under Chapter 96 during a public
emergency.
(Prior Code, § 29.01.01)
   (B)   Establishment of emergency response team. There is hereby established
an Emergency Response Team to assist the Mayor of the city during times of
public emergency. The Emergency Response Team shall consist of the following:
      (1)   Mayor;
      (2)   President of the Council;
      (3)   Vice President of the Council;
      (4)   Finance Officer or designee and Secretary;
      (5)   Chief of Police or designee and Secretary;
      (6)   Public Works Director or designee and Secretary;
      (7)   City Attorney or designee;
      (8)   Head of Water Department or designee;
      (9)   Head of Parks Department or designee; and
      (10)   Fire and Emergency Director or designee.
(Prior Code, § 29.02.01)
   (C)   Establishment of Office of Emergency Coordinator.
      (1)   There is hereby established an Office of Emergency Coordinator.
      (2)   The duties of the Emergency Coordinator are to assist the Mayor and
city officials in coordinating all efforts during an emergency. A Coordinator
should be allowed, as it is necessary, to see to it that all efforts of an
emergency are properly executed in cooperation with other city departments,
state, county or federal officials.
      (3)   The Coordinator shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. Said
Coordinator shall receive no salary but may be reimbursed such costs and
expenses as the City Council may deem reasonable.
(Prior Code, § 29.02.02)
   (D)   Powers of emergency response team. The Emergency Response Team shall
have such powers as are necessary to organize and coordinate all efforts during
an emergency or in the event of imminent danger to public safety. Further, said
Emergency Response Team may enact such regulations, policy handbooks and
procedure manuals in handling emergencies in the city as it deems necessary.
(Prior Code, § 29.02.03)
   (E)   Headquarters. The Emergency Response Team may designate one place as
headquarters for city services during an emergency.
(Prior Code, § 29.02.04)
   (F)   Official spokesperson. The Mayor may appoint one person as the
official spokesperson for the city during times of imminent danger to public
safety or emergency. Said person shall be responsible for handling all official
news releases, press conferences or information to be disseminated to the media
or public.
(Prior Code, § 29.02.05)
   (G)   Budget. The City Council may set a budget for expenses incurred by the
Emergency Response Team.
(Prior Code, § 29.02.06)
(Ord. 2007-32, passed 9-21-2007) Penalty, see §
32.99
§ 32.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person violating any provision of this chapter for which no
specific penalty is prescribed shall be subject to §
10.99.
   (B)   Any violation of the provisions of §
32.30 is a Class 2 misdemeanor punishable by the maximum punishment set forth
by the laws of the state pursuant to SDCL § 22-6-2. Said punishment may also
include payment of any costs and/or restitution authorized by this code and/or
state law.
(Prior Code, § 29.01.03)
CHAPTER 33: CITY PERSONNEL
Section
   
33.01   Personnel policy
   
33.02   Code of conduct under federal grants
§ 33.01 PERSONNEL POLICY.
   (A)   Definition. All persons performing services for the city and who are
not appointive officers of the city are CITY EMPLOYEES.
   (B)   Employment-at-will. South Dakota is an “employment-at-will” state.
Subject to certain common law limitations and public policy exceptions, an at-
will employment may be terminated at-will, with or without cause at any time.
The intent of the city is to maintain employment at-will status of all
employees.
   (C)   Personnel policy manual.
      (1)   The city may by resolution adopt a personnel policy manual for the
purpose of regulating those matters relating to city employees as the City
Council may approve; provided, that the personnel policy manual does not
contain any provision inconsistent with the employment-at-will status of city
employees; and further provided that the personnel policies are subject to such
provisions as the City Council may approve in any collective bargaining
agreement.
      (2)   The personnel policy manual is not an employment contract. The
policies, procedures, rules and benefits contained in the personnel policy
manual are subject to change upon a majority vote of the City Council. The
policies are provided as a reference to present policies and not a guarantee of
employment or any specific employment benefit.
   (D)   Employee classification; positions authorized. Employees of the city
are classified as salaried, hourly, exempt and nonexempt in conformance with
applicable state and federal law. The employee positions within the city and
its departments to which personnel may be hired, and the compensation
authorized for each such position, are as authorized by the City Council.
   (E)   Employee wages and benefits. Employee wage rates and salaries,
including any step plan or wage or salary gradations or wage and salary
graduations, are determined by resolution of the City Council, or notations in
the minutes of a City Council meeting. Employee benefits supplemental to wages
and salary area also as determined by the City Council. Except as may be
contained in a collective bargaining contract, no such employee wage or benefit
determination or wage and benefit determination is contractual.
   (F)   Employee retirement system. All ordinances establishing retirement
system(s) for city employees within the state retirement system are maintained
and not repealed by the enactment of this code.
(Prior Code, § 7.05.01) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012)
§ 33.02 CODE OF CONDUCT UNDER FEDERAL GRANTS.
   (A)   Purpose. The purpose of this code of conduct is to ensure the
efficient, fair and professional administration of federal grant funds in
compliance with the Federal Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-
102, Attachment O, Paragraph 7 and other applicable federal and state
standards, regulations and laws.
   (B)   Application of provisions. This code of conduct applies to all
officers, employees or agents of the city engaged in the award or
administration of contracts supported by federal grant funds.
   (C)   Requirements.
      (1)   No officer, employee or agent of the city may participate in the
selection, award or administration of a contract supported by federal grant
funds if a conflict of interest, real or apparent, is involved. Such a conflict
arises when any employee, officer or agent, any members of the employees,
officers or agent’s immediate family, a partner or an organization which
employs or is about to employ any of the above has a financial or other
interest in the firm selected for the award.
      (2)   The city’s officers, employees or agents must neither solicit nor
accept gratuities, favors or anything of monetary value from contractors,
potential contractors or subcontractors.
   (D)   Remedies. To the extent allowed by federal, state law, state or this
code, local laws or other regulations, violation of these standards may cause
penalties, sanctions or other disciplinary actions to be taken against the
city’s officers, employees or agents or the contractors, potential contractors,
subcontractors or other agents.
(Prior Code, § 7.05.02) (Ord. 2012-16, passed 12-5-2012) Penalty, see §
10.99
