**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 110.001 SCOPE AND PURPOSE.
   This chapter shall set forth licensing requirements related to the sale of
alcohol and malt beverages and shall regulate drinking establishments and the
sale of alcohol and malt beverages within the city.
(Prior Code, § 3.01.01)
§ 110.002 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning. If a term
is not defined in this section or elsewhere in this chapter, the term is to be
given the meaning as defined in SDCL Title 35.
   ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE. Any distilled spirits, wine and malt beverages as
defined in this chapter.
   BAR. Any permanent installed counter within the restaurant area from which
alcoholic beverages are regularly served to customers by a person employed by
the facility and is tending bar or drawing or mixing or otherwise preparing
alcoholic beverages for consumption within the facility.
   BUILDING/STRUCTURE. Structure having a roof supported by columns or walls
for the shelter, support or enclosure for persons, animals or property. A
BUILDING may be precut or prefabricated, or it may be made up of mobile modules
or sections, factory fabricated and transportable by rail or truck to a
building site and designed to be incorporated into a structure upon a permanent
foundation on said site.
   BULK CONTAINER. Any package or any container within which container is one
or more packages.
   BUSINESS. Any activity, trade, calling, profession or occupation, whether
sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, limited liability company or
other recognized entity, which regularly provides delivery of products and/or
services from an address or other location(s) within the corporate limits of
the city. BUSINESS includes HOME OCCUPATIONS which involve the sale of goods or
services as described in this definition.
   CHARITABLE ORGANIZATION. Any state recognized or I.R.C. § 501(c)(3) not-for-
profit organization (either a private foundation or public charity) that is
organized and operated exclusively for established philanthropic, humanitarian,
altruistic, benevolent, public-spirited, scientific, literary or religious
purposes, including, but not limited to, relief of the poor, the distressed or
the underprivileged; advancement of religion; advancement of education or
science; erecting or maintaining public buildings, monuments or works;
lessening the burdens of government; lessening neighborhood tensions;
eliminating prejudice and discrimination; defending human and civil rights
secured by law; and combating community deterioration and juvenile delinquency.
    CIVIC ORGANIZATION. Any state recognized or I.R.C. § 501(c)(4) not-for-
profit organization or league not organized for profit but operated exclusively
for the promotion of social welfare or for the purpose of serving a public or
mutual benefit within or to the community. Also, alternatively, any local
association of persons, the membership of which is limited to the persons in
the city and the net earnings of which are devoted exclusively to charitable,
education or recreational purposes in the city.
   DISTILLED SPIRITS. Ethyl alcohol, hydrated oxide of ethyl, spirits of wine,
whiskey, rum, brandy, gin and other distilled spirits, including all dilutions
and mixtures thereof, for nonindustrial use, containing not less than 0.5% of
alcohol by weight.
   EDUCATIONAL ORGANIZATION. Any state recognized or I.R.C. § 501(c)(3) not-
for-profit organization that is organized and operated exclusively for
established educational purposes, encompassing individual instruction, as well
as public instruction on subjects useful to the individual and beneficial to
the community.
   EVENT. An organized occurrence or happening lasting four or more consecutive
days or where the city provides extraordinary services, including, but not
limited to, sanitation services, law enforcement or traffic control. This
definition does not apply to a special event license described below.
   FRATERNAL ORGANIZATION. Any state recognized or I.R.C. §§ 501(c)(8) or 501
(c)(10) not-for-profit organization that is organized and operated for a
fraternal purpose and whose membership is based on a common tie or the pursuit
of a common object. A FRATERNAL ORGANIZATION must operate under a lodge system.
   FLOOR. An area that is surrounded by exterior walls and a roof of the
building or portion thereof.
   MALT BEVERAGE. A beverage made by the alcoholic fermentation of an infusion
or decoction, or combination of both, in potable brewing water, of malted
barley with hops, or their parts, or their products, and with or without other
malted cereals, and with or without the addition of unmalted or prepared
cereals, other carbohydrates or products prepared therefrom, and with or
without the addition of carbon dioxide, and with or without other wholesome
products suitable for human consumption containing not less than 0.5% of
alcohol by weight.
   MINOR. Any person who is under the age of 21.
   OFF-SALE. The sale of any alcoholic beverage for consumption off the
premises where sold.
   ON-SALE. The sale of any alcoholic beverage for consumption only upon the
premises where it is sold.
   ON-SALE DEALER. Any person who sells, or keeps for sale, any alcoholic
beverage for consumption on the premises where sold.
   OPERATION. In action, functioning.
   PACKAGE. The bottle or immediate container of any alcoholic beverage.
   PACKAGE DEALER. Any person other than a distiller, manufacturer or
wholesaler, who sells, or keeps for sale, any alcoholic beverage for
consumption off the premises where sold.
   PUBLIC PLACE. Any location that the local, state or national government
maintains for the use of the public, such as a highway, park or public
building.
   RESTAURANT. A room and/or structure regularly, and in bona fide manner, used
and kept open for the serving and/or preparing of meals to guests for
compensation which has suitable table accommodations for at least 50 guests
therein at one and the same time; and a kitchen connected therewith containing
conveniences for cooking sufficient to provide preparation and cooking of meals
in a bona fide manner for 50 or more guests at one and the same time.
Facilities who serve only prepackage foods or items that can be heated in a
microwave or small pizza or toaster ovens will not be considered a RESTAURANT.
   RETAIL LICENSE. Any on-sale or off-sale license issued under the provisions
of this chapter.
   RETAILER or RETAIL DEALER. Any person who sells alcoholic beverages for
other than resale.
   ROOF. Any structural element or group of elements which are structural in
nature and are covered with a material(s) that is (are) weather resistant. The
ROOF shall be the top most element of the structure that meets the requirements
of the current adopted Building Code.
   SALE. The transfer, for a consideration, of title to any alcoholic beverage.
   SPECIAL EVENT. 
      (1)   An event or activity occurring or to be conducted within the city
by a generally recognized:
         (a)   Civic organization with an active chapter located within the
city;
         (b)   Charitable organization with an active chapter located within
the city;
         (c)   Educational organization with an active chapter located within
the city;
         (d)   Fraternal organization with an active chapter located; or
         (e)   Veteran’s organization with an active chapter located within the
city.
      (2)   In addition, a SPECIAL EVENT may include an event to be conducted
by a licensee, holding a license issued by the city pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2
(4), (12) or (16), for the following purposes:
         (a)   A recognized event linked to developing and encouraging tourism
in the community and/or county; or
         (b)   A recognized event within the city or county which is not
primarily intended or planned to increase tourism activities but which the City
Council finds would be of benefit to the citizens of the community.
   SPECIAL EVENT ON-SALE LICENSE. 
      (1)   For purposes of obtaining a special event on-sale license, a
special event within the municipality is defined as an event or activity to be
conducted within the city by a generally recognized:
         (a)   Civic organization with an active chapter located within the
city;
         (b)   Charitable organization with an active chapter located within
the city;
         (c)   Educational organization with an active chapter located within
the city;
         (d)   Fraternal organization with an active chapter located within the
city; or
         (e)   Veteran’s organization with an active chapter located within the
city, or an event where a licensee already holding an on-sale license issued by
the city pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2(4), (12) or (16) applies for and receives
approval from the Common Council:
            1.   A recognized event linked to developing and encouraging
tourism in the community and county; or
            2.   A recognized event within the city or county which is not
primarily planned to increase tourism activities but which the City Council
finds would be of benefit to the citizens of the community.
      (2)   To obtain the SPECIAL EVENT LICENSE, the applicant shall submit an
application stating the qualifications for a special event license on a form
consistent with the requirements of SDCL § 35-4-124, and providing all
additional information required by the City Finance Office to meet the
requirements of this chapter. A SPECIAL EVENT LICENSE may only be issued to a
current city license holder only for the same class of license previously
issued to the licensee by the city.
   TO SELL AND SERVE ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES. To take orders for alcoholic
beverages and to deliver alcoholic beverages to customers as a normal adjunct
of waiting tables. This term does not include tending bar or drawing or mixing
alcoholic beverages.
   WALL. Any wall or element of a wall, or any member or group of members,
structural or non-structural, which defines the boundaries of a building and
which is opaque in nature with the exception of windows or doors and supports a
roof and/or floor above.
   WINE. Any liquid either commonly used, or reasonably adapted to use, for
beverage purposes, and obtained by the fermentation of the natural sugar
content of fruits or other agricultural products containing sugar and
containing not less than 0.5% of alcohol by weight but not more than 24% of
alcohol by weight.
   VETERANS ORGANIZATION. Any bona fide congressionally chartered veterans
organization.
(Prior Code, § 3.01.02) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
**** LICENSING AND SALES ****
§ 110.015 LICENSE REQUIRED.
   (A)   No person shall sell, keep for sale, exchange, barter or distribute
any alcoholic or malt beverage without having obtained a license as required by
the provisions of the State Liquor Control Law, SDCL Title 35, and by this
chapter.
   (B)   Any person who intends to sell, keep for sale, exchange, barter or
distribute any alcoholic or malt beverage shall make an application for license
under provisions of the State Liquor Control Law, SDCL Title 35, to the City
Finance Officer.
   (C)   Upon issuance of said license, the licensee shall be given a copy of
this chapter and sign a statement verifying that he or she has received a copy
of this chapter. It shall be the responsibility of each licensee to acknowledge
in writing he, she or they have read and understood this chapter. Any violation
of this chapter shall be subject to the general penalty set out at §
110.999.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.01) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.016 WHOLESALE LICENSE FEE.
   (A)   The city does hereby impose a fee of 5% of the wholesale purchase
price, plus freight, for all malt beverages as defined by SDCL § 35-1-1, as
amended, delivered to the following persons:
      (1)   Any person holding a malt beverage retailer’s license, issued
pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2(16);
      (2)   Any person holding a malt beverage package dealer’s license, issued
pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2(17); or
      (3)   Any person holding a special malt beverage retailer’s license,
issued pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-11.4.
   (B)   The authority for the imposition of this fee is contained in SDCL §
35-4-60.2.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.02)
§ 110.017 SUBMISSION OF INVOICES AND ASSESSMENT OF FEES.
   (A)   All malt beverage wholesalers, as defined by SDCL § 35-1-1, and
licensed, pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2, shall provide a copy to the Finance
Officer of all invoices for sales of malt beverages delivered to the malt
beverage dealers, as described in §
110.016, within the city, on or before the fifth day of each month for all
sales made in the city for the prior month.
   (B)   The Finance Officer shall on the fifteenth day of each month, or on
the first working day thereafter, send a statement to each malt beverage
dealer, assessing the fee required hereunder, based upon all invoices received
by the city for malt beverages delivered to the dealer for the prior calendar
month. The dealer shall have a period of ten days within which to pay to the
city the fee required hereunder. In the event of the failure by the dealer to
pay the required fee within said ten-day time period, the Finance Officer shall
notify the malt beverage wholesalers, in writing, by first-class mail, postage
prepaid, of the fact that this fee has not been paid and that the license
holder is in violation of the terms of this chapter. A copy of the notice sent
to the malt beverage wholesaler shall be sent to the dealer who is in default.
The wholesalers shall not deliver any malt beverage to the dealer who is in
default under the terms of this chapter until such time as the wholesalers are
notified by the city that all fees owing to the city have been paid in full.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.03)
§ 110.018 DELIVERY AND SALE REQUIRED WITHIN CITY.
   No malt beverage dealer, as described in §
110.016, shall sell any malt beverages that have not been delivered to the malt
beverage dealer within the city for sale within the city.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.04) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.019 CONSEQUENCES FOR FAILURE TO TIMELY PAY CITY.
   (A)   No malt beverage dealer’s license, as described in §
110.016, shall be renewed until all fees owing pursuant to this chapter have
been paid in full.
   (B)   In addition to the termination of the malt beverage sales to the
premises affected and/or non-renewal of a license, the city may take any civil
action authorized by the statutes of the state to collect the charges imposed
by this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.05) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.020 MAINTENANCE OF RECORDS AND INSPECTION BY DEALER.
   (A)   The Finance Officer shall maintain an accurate record, using the
information supplied by the malt beverage wholesaler of the sales made to the
individual malt beverage dealers in the city.
   (B)   The records, including copies of wholesalers’ invoices, maintained by
the Finance Officer concerning any malt beverage dealer shall be open to
inspection only by that dealer or his or her designee during normal business
hours.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.06)
§ 110.021 LIMITATION OF ONE LICENSE PER LOCATION.
   No person shall hold both a retail on-sale liquor license, issued pursuant
to SDCL § 35-4-2(4) and a retail malt beverage on/off-sale and state farm wine
license issued pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2(16) and (17), for the same location.
However, a person holding a malt beverage manufactures license and an on-sale
liquor license for the same premises, and open to the public at least six days
a week for 11 months a year, may hold a malt beverage retailer license to sell
for off-sale consumption of the malt beverage it manufactures, but only at the
licensed premises at which the malt beverage is manufactured.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.07) Penalty, see §
110.999

§ 110.023 SPECIAL EVENT LICENSE REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   A special retail malt beverage on-/off-sale and state farm wine
license may be issued in conjunction with a special event, as defined at §
110.002, within the city to any qualified civic, charitable, educational,
fraternal or veterans organization or any qualified licensee licensed pursuant
to SDCL § 35-4-2(4), (6) or (16) in addition to any other licenses held by the
special events license applicant.
   (B)   A special retail on-off sale wine and cider license may be issued in
conjunction with a special event, as defined in §
110.002, within the city to any qualified civic, charitable, educational,
fraternal or veterans organization or any qualified licensee licensed pursuant
to SDCL § 35-4-2(4), (6) or (12) or SDCL Chapter 35-12 in addition to any other
licenses held by the special events license applicant.
   (C)   A special retail on-sale liquor license may be issued in conjunction
with a special event, as defined in §
110.002, within the city to any qualified civic, charitable, educational,
fraternal or veterans organization or any qualified licensee licensed pursuant
to SDCL § 35-4-2(4), (6) or (16) in addition to any other licenses held by the
special events license applicant.
   (D)   The daily fee for each special event retail malt beverage on/off-sale
and state farm wine license, special event retail (on-/off-sale) wine and cider
license that is issued shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution.
The daily fee for each special event retail on-sale liquor license that is
issued shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution.
   (E)   A public hearing is required before approval and issuance of any
license under this section.
   (F)   Any licenses issued pursuant to this section may be issued for a
period of time established by the City Council not exceeding 15 consecutive
days.
   (G)   Any nonprofit licensee under this section may not be issued more than
five special event licenses for a total of 15 days during a single calendar
year. Any current licensee may not be issued more than 30 special event
licenses during a single calendar year.
   (H)   This license may be issued pursuant all additional requirements of
SDCL § 35-4-124, including the procedural regulations adopted by a resolution
of the Council.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.09)
§ 110.024 CONSUMPTION ONLY PERMIT.
   (A)   The fee for this permit shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee
resolution.
   (B)   This permit allows the applicant to provide alcoholic beverages free
of charge during the applicant’s rental or use of city facilities or
properties.
   (C)   The application permit must be completed and filed with the Finance
Office at least 30 days prior to the first day of proposed rental or use of a
city facility or property and must be accompanied by a signed rental agreement
and other documents required by city policy.
   (D)   The applicant must be at least 21 years of age and provide an
acceptable form of identification, together with a signed hold harmless
agreement.
   (E)   This permit allows, with City Council’s approval, the consumption of
any alcoholic beverages on the city property or by an individual or a nonprofit
corporation within the city. The length of the consumption permit may not
exceed 24 hours. Hours of consumption may not exceed those permitted for on-
sale licensees.
   (F)   The applicant must have at least the amount as shall be set forth in
the city’s annual fee resolution in liability insurance coverage for the
permit. A statement from applicant’s insurance carrier confirming coverage for
the proposed site and naming the city as co-insured shall be provided with the
application or it will be denied as an incomplete application.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.10)

(Prior Code, § 3.02.11)
§ 110.026 RETAIL (ON-/OFF-SALE) MALT BEVERAGE AND STATE FARM WINE LICENSE
PROVISIONS.
   The City Council, through its authority under SDCL § 35-4-11, removes any
prior maximum number of retail (on/off) malt beverage and state farm licenses
established. In lieu of the provision disestablishing the maximum number of
malt beverage and state farm wine licenses, the City Council may, by resolution
passed before September 2, establish a limit on the number of licenses the
Council will approve for the ensuing calendar year. If the City Council does
not pass a resolution setting the number of licenses and/or fees as provided in
this section, then the most recent resolution passed under this section sets
the number and/or fees. If no prior resolution set the prescribed number or
fees, or the resolution has been repealed, then this section or any applicable
section under this chapter applies. Any on-/off-sale restaurant malt beverage
licenses issued by the city are hereby transferred to and now known as retail
(on-/off-sale) malt beverage and state farm wine licenses, and subject to the
license limitations provided by this section. All licensees shall be located in
an area zoned for commercial or agricultural use and with the proposed
premises, including a permanent structure of at least 1,200 square feet on
property owned or leased by the licensees.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.12) (Ord. 2024-04, passed 7-19-2024)
§ 110.027 AUTHORIZED NUMBER OF OFF-SALE LIQUOR LICENSES.
   In recognition of the authority granted by the legislature under SDCL § 35-
4-10, the Council has authorized the issuance of two off-sale licenses for the
sale of distilled spirits within the city. Both such license shall continue to
be held by the city.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.13) (Ord. 2015-13, passed 12-2-2015)
§ 110.028 SALES ON SUNDAY OR MEMORIAL DAY PURSUANT TO STATUTE.
   Off-sale or on-sale licensees holding valid licenses within the city may,
pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-81.2, sell alcoholic beverages on Sunday and also on
Memorial Day within the municipality during hours otherwise allowed by state
statute.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.14) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.029 ACTION BY COUNCIL.
   The Common Council may approve or disapprove an application for a license or
a special event license depending on whether the Council finds the applicant a
suitable person to hold the license and whether the Council considers the
proposed location suitable. The Common Council may, in its discretion, require
the applicant to appear personally at any meeting of the Council and to answer
any question which may be asked pertaining to the applicant or the place of
business which may in any way pertain to the carrying on of the business
applied for.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.15)
§ 110.030 CHARACTER REQUIREMENTS FOR LICENSE.
   Any licensee or special event license under this chapter and SDCL Title 35
must be a person of good moral character, who has never been convicted of a
felony. If the licensee is a corporation, the managing officers thereof must
have like qualifications.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.16)
§ 110.031 AREA LIMITED.
   The Common Council shall not approve any application for “on-sale” or “off-
sale” license to sell any alcoholic beverages in the city at any place of
business unless that place of business is located in an area zoned as a
commercial or agricultural area on the zoning use district map of the city. The
Common Council may approve a waiver of this requirement by approving a
temporary exemption for an off-sale license, or by approving an on-sale special
event license, for a period not to exceed 15 days, as provided for in §
110.023.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.17) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.032 KEGS OF MALT BEVERAGE; RETAIL SALE; RECORDS.
   (A)   No keg of malt beverage may be sold at retail in this state unless the
licensee who sold the keg records the name address and driver’s license number
of the person to whom the keg is sold and has provided for the identification
of the keg. Each licensee shall maintain such sales records for one year and
shall make the records upon request to any duly authorized officer or
representative of any city, county or state agency responsible for enforcing
this section or for enforcing state codified laws pertaining to consumption of
alcohol.
   (B)   The identification provided for in this section may not be permanent
or damaging to the structure of the keg. For the purpose of this section, the
term KEG means an eight- or 16-gallon reusable plastic or metal container.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.18)
§ 110.033 CONSUMING, BLENDING, POSSESSING ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES IN PUBLIC PLACES;
DISPOSAL OF CONTAINERS OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES RESTRICTED.
   (A)   It is unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverage upon
the premises of a licensed on-sale dealer if the alcoholic beverage was not
purchased from the on-sale dealer.
   (B)   It is unlawful for any person to consume any alcoholic beverages in
any public place, other than upon the premises of a licensed on-sale dealer.
For the purpose of this section, the term PUBLIC PLACE means any place, whether
in or out of a building, commonly and customarily open to or used by the
general public, and any street or highway.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.19) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.034 OPEN CONTAINERS PERMITTED UPON APPROVAL.
   (A)   No regular on-sale malt beverage licensee may sell or allow to be
consumed any malt beverage outside the building of the licensed premises unless
the business operates out of a permanent structure and the consumption of the
malt beverage occurs in an outdoor designated area located on the licensed
premises of the licensee.
   (B)   (1)   The sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages may be permitted
on a sidewalk or walkway within a public right-of-way if that sidewalk area
abuts a licensed premises, provided that the license holder derives more than
50% of its gross receipts from the sale of food prepared for consumption on the
licensed premises. The sidewalk or walkway subject to a public right-of-way
shall be immediately adjacent to and abutting the licensed premises. This
section does not apply to any federal-aid eligible highway unless approved in
accordance with the applicable requirements for the receipt of federal aid and
does not waive the requirements set out in §
151.007.
      (2)   In place of the process described in §
130.024, an area for open container shall only be established as described in
this division (B). Upon receipt of a completed application and fee as shall be
set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution, the Finance Officer will place
the request on the Council meeting agenda to set a public hearing as provided
by statute. The application to the City Finance Office shall be on a form
approved by that Office, accompanied by the required fee, and include or be
accompanied by the following information:
         (a)   The applicant’s name, address and phone number;
         (b)   A copy of the insurance coverage applicant has obtained for the
event;
         (c)   A statement of the purpose and community benefit for which the
closure is being requested;
         (d)   A detailed description of the street or other public area the
applicant is requesting be closed as an open container area; and
         (e)   The date and time for which the applicant is requesting closure
for an open container area.
      (3)   After completion of the public hearing the City Council may, by
resolution, close off an area of public right-of-way or public area as defined
by SDCL § 35-1-5.3 and designate it as an open container area for a special
event. In the event that any area of a public street is closed by such
resolution of the City Council, said area shall not be construed as a public
place, as that term is defined in §
110.033. The restrictions upon open containers set forth in this chapter shall
not be enforced within said area during the time frame of closure set forth in
the resolution. The time for consumption within the open container area, as
defined in the resolution, may not exceed the hours of consumption permitted
for on-sale licensees. The time frame may not exceed ten consecutive days.
   (C)   The Common Council may, in its discretion, for community designated
events, permit open containers in public places upon the terms and conditions
stated in its resolution which it finds are consistent with the laws of the
state and this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.20) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.035 WEAPONS PROHIBITED ON PREMISES WHERE SOLD.
   All license holders shall post the following notice at all entrances to
their establishment in bold capital letters at least three-fourths of an inch
high.
 
It Is Unlawful to Enter this Establishment with Any Weapon.
 
(Prior Code, § 3.02.21) Penalty, see §

§ 110.036 ANNUAL REVIEW OF APPLICATIONS.
   Annually, the City Council shall review each completed application for malt
beverage and/or alcohol licenses. Issuance of any license or special event
license shall be subject to a determination by City Council as to whether or
not the permanent structure on the premises and the proposed location is
fitting for the type of business that has been presented and is proposed to be
operated at the legal description set forth in the application submitted
pursuant to §
110.015. The City Council shall take into consideration the location of any new
or transferred license and its location in relationship to any residentially
zoned area, school, daycare, church, place of worship and/or similar uses and
such other location issues as the City Council may deem appropriate in
reviewing and issuing a new or transferred license.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.22) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.037 SALES WITH LICENSE ONLY.
   Malt beverage and/or alcohol may be sold and/or consumed only at locations
shown on the license issued by the city and is on file with the City Finance
Officer and the State Department of Revenue. Property for which a permanent
license is in existence at the time of adoption of this chapter shall be
permitted to continue their operations as they have in the past until said time
that the license has been transferred or revoked by the City Council. In
addition, these properties shall comply with the regulations, which were in
effect at the time of issuance of their license.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.23)
§ 110.038 ADDITIONAL FEE FOR VIDEO LOTTERY MACHINE HOLDERS.
   An additional license fee is hereby imposed in the amount as shall be set
forth in the city’s annual fee resolution for each video lottery machine on the
licensed premises, which fee shall be applicable to all classes of licenses
enumerated under SDCL § 35-4-2(4), (11), (14) and (17), which involve
convention facility, on-sale and malt beverage retailers; provided, that not
more than one fee shall be imposed per location, and the fee shall be paid at
the same time and in the same manner as the fees paid on licenses issued
pursuant to SDCL § 35-4-2. All fees received under this section shall be
deposited into the General Fund of the city.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.24)
§ 110.039 TRAFFIC IN ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES PROHIBITED.
   No person shall produce, transport, store or sell any alcoholic beverage
except as authorized under the provisions of this chapter and SDCL Title 35.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.25) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.040 PERSONS UNDER 21 BARRED FROM ON-SALE PREMISES.
   As prohibited by SDCL § 35-4-79, no on-sale licensee shall permit any person
less than 21 years old to loiter on the licensed premises or to sell, serve,
dispense or consume alcoholic beverages on such premises, unless the presence
of the person under the age of 21 is authorized by the exception language of
either SDCL §§ 9-1-1 or 9-1-1.1.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.26) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.041 VIOLATION AS GROUND FOR REVOCATION OF SUSPENSION OF LICENSE; MULTIPLE
LICENSES.
   (A)   The Common Council may recommend any license issued under this chapter
and/or SDCL Title 35 be revoked or suspended upon proof of violation by the
licensee, by the licensee’s agents or employees or by the manager or
contractual operators of retail establishments and their agents or employees
operating under a city license, of any of the following:
      (1)   Any provision of SDCL Title 35;
      (2)   Any rule promulgated pursuant to SDCL Title 35; or
      (3)   Any ordinance or regulation relevant to alcoholic beverage control
that has been adopted by the city.
   (B)   For any licensee with multiple alcoholic beverage licenses for the
same premises, upon suspension or revocation of any license issued pursuant to
this chapter or SDCL Title 35, such licensee shall cease operation under all
alcoholic beverage licenses held by such licensee for the same premises for the
same period as the suspension or revocation.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.27) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
**** FULL-SERVICE ON-SALE AND MALT BEVERAGE RESTAURANT LICENSES ****
§ 110.055 LICENSE APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   An applicant for a full-service restaurant on-sale license shall
provide sufficient documentation to the municipality with an application form
provided by the municipality to prove that the primary source of revenue from
the operation of the restaurant will be derived from the sale of prepared food
and nonalcoholic beverages and not from the sale of alcoholic beverages.
   (B)   The supporting documentation concerning the primary source of revenue
submitted pursuant to this section is confidential.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.01) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.056 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   BAR. Any permanently installed counter within the restaurant area from which
alcoholic beverages are regularly served to customers by a person who is
tending bar or drawing or mixing alcoholic beverages.
   FULL-SERVICE RESTAURANT. Any restaurant at which a waiter or waitress
delivers food and drink offered from a printed food menu to patrons at tables,
booths or the bar. Any restaurant that only serves fry orders or food such as
sandwiches, hamburgers or salads is not a FULL-SERVICE RESTAURANT.
   RESTAURANT. Any area in a building maintained, advertised and held out to
the public as a place where individually priced meals are prepared and served
primarily for consumption in such area and where not more than 40% of the gross
revenue of the restaurant is derived from the sale of alcohol or alcoholic
beverages. The RESTAURANT shall have a dining room or rooms, a kitchen and the
number and kinds of employees necessary for the preparing, cooking and serving
of meals.
   SPA AND/OR HEALTH AND BEAUTY ESTABLISHMENT. Any establishment licensed under
SDCL Chapter 36-15, such as a nail or hair business.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.02) (Ord. 2016-01, passed 6-1-2016)
§ 110.057 ANNUAL REPORT.
   (A)   The full-service restaurant on-sale licensee shall submit an annual
report and supporting documentation to the city on forms provided by the City
Finance Office of the annual sales of the full-service restaurant, which
includes an oath verifying the validity of the information provided in the
report.
   (B)   The report and the supporting documentation submitted pursuant to this
section are confidential.
   (C)   The report shall contain the annual gross sales of the licensee for
the following two categories:
      (1)   Food and nonalcoholic beverage sales; and
      (2)   Alcoholic beverage sales.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.03) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.058 LICENSE RENEWAL.
   When renewing a full-service restaurant on-sale license, the city shall
condition the license renewal upon receiving documentation that not more than
40% of gross sales from the preceding 12 months operation of the full-service
restaurant is derived from the sale of alcohol or alcoholic beverages.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.04) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.059 ONLY RETAIL, ON-SALE SERVICE PERMITTED.
   A full-service restaurant on-sale licensee may only serve alcoholic
beverages for on-premises consumption in the bar and dining room area of the
restaurant.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.05)
§ 110.060 FULL-SERVICE RESTAURANT LICENSE FEE.
   As required by state law, the license fee charged for a full-service
restaurant on-sale license shall be at or above the current fair market value
for such license as determined herein.
   (A)   For the purpose of this section, the term CURRENT FAIR MARKET VALUE
means the documented price of the on-sale license most recently sold, through
an arm’s-length transaction, less the value of any real or personal property
included in the transaction, to determine the amount paid by the licensee for
the on-sale license. If there are no documented sales of on-sale licenses
contained in the records of the City Finance Office, the city may request from
any on-sale license holder within the city the date and price originally paid
for its on-sale license to determine current fair market value.
   (B)   Any form submitted to establish current fair market pursuant to this
provision shall be signed under oath and shall include the documents
establishing the amount originally paid for the on-sale license. Current fair
market value as determined by the Council shall be a minimum amount as shall be
set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution for each person residing within
the city as measured by the last preceding decennial federal census.
   (C)   The license fee shall be established by Council resolution, including
its determination of current fair market value, to be adopted within 90 days of
a revision to this section. Subsequent changes in the license fee shall not be
made for a period of ten years from the effective date of adoption of the
Council resolution unless a population growth reported by the federal decennial
census requires an increase in the fee. A city licensee under this chapter may
contest the Council’s determination of current fair market value contained in
the Council resolution by using the appeal process.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.06) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.061 REGISTRY OF FULL-SERVICE RESTAURANT ON-SALE LICENSEES.
   (A)   The City Finance Office shall notify each current on-sale license
holder of the existence of the registry and then maintain a registry of each
full-service on-sale restaurant license that is being offered for sale. The
city shall furnish a copy of the registry to anyone who requests a new-full
service restaurant on-sale license.
   (B)   After receiving this notification, the existing full-service
restaurant on-sale licensee is responsible for registering with the city that
the full-service restaurant on-sale license is for sale.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.07)
§ 110.062 ISSUANCE OF NEW FULL-SERVICE RESTAURANT LICENSE RESTRICTED.
   The city may only issue a new license pursuant to this subchapter if no on-
sale license is on the registry or a person desiring to purchase an on-sale
license listed on the registry provides documentation showing that the person
is unable to purchase the on-sale license at the price established pursuant to
this subchapter and on terms satisfactory to both the potential buyer and
seller. The price of any on-sale license registered as “for sale” with the city
shall be sold at the current fair market price set by the city pursuant to a
resolution adopted in accordance with this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.08)
§ 110.063 SPA AND/OR HEALTH AND BEAUTY RETAIL ON-/OFF-SALE MALT BEVERAGE AND
WINE LICENSES.
   Spa and/or health and beauty establishments licensed under SDCL Chapter 36-
15 and in good standing with the state may apply for a retail on-/off-sale malt
beverage license. This shall be subject to the temporary use inspection period
and process as described in §
156.394.
(Prior Code, § 3.03.12) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
**** STRUCTURE REQUIREMENTS, ON-SALE ESTABLISHMENTS ****
§ 110.075 MANDATORY COMPLIANCE WITH STATE AND LOCAL LICENSING LAWS.
   (A)   No person shall sell, keep for sale, exchange, barter or distribute
any alcoholic or malt beverage without having obtained a license pursuant to
the provisions of the State Liquor Control Law (SDCL Title 35) and this
chapter.
    (B)   Any person who intends to sell, keep for sale, exchange, barter or
distribute any alcoholic or malt beverage shall make an application for license
under provisions of the State Liquor Control Law (SDCL Title 35) and to the
City Finance Officer.
   (C)   All malt beverage and/or alcohol licenses may be issued only if the
proposed license is in compliance with in zoning requirements and all other
city ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.01) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.076 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS AND/OR LIMITATIONS.
   (A)   All federal, state and local laws shall be complied with at all times.
   (B)   In the event a fight or civil disturbance occurs within the temporary
drinking establishment where police are called to assist, the establishment
shall temporarily cease selling of all malt beverage/alcohol until the
disturbance is under control and the City Police Department has granted
permission to reestablish sales.
   (C)   Beverage cans, trash and other debris which is collected during an
event shall be bagged and removed from the property on a daily basis to prevent
the accumulation of pests and to deter unwanted smell as required by §§
50.035 through
50.048.
   (D)   It shall be unlawful for any person to permit illegal nudity, lewd or
indecent acts, exhibitions or any other behavior in violation of §§
94.150 through
94.164 to take place within their establishment.
   (E)   Any structure from which alcoholic beverages are sold or served shall
be constructed in compliance with this chapter and all city building and/or
fire codes and other applicable ordinances.
   (F)   It shall be unlawful for any person to allow the distribution, sale
and/or consumption of malt beverage and/or alcohol by a minor in their
establishment.
   (G)   No person who has been issued a license for alcoholic beverages under
this chapter may permit any illegal activity within the licensed premises or on
adjoining property subject to the control of the licensee.
   (H)   No person who has been issued a malt beverage and/or alcohol license
shall permit prostitution as prohibited by SDCL Chapter 22-23. In addition to
the penalty set forth in this chapter, any persons who permits illegal
prostitution to take place within their drinking establishment shall be subject
to possible revocation or non-renewal of their malt beverage and/or alcohol
license.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.02) Penalty, see §
110.999
§ 110.077 CONSTRUCTION REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   All structures utilized for drinking establishments after the adoption
of this chapter shall comply with the current adopted addition of the
International Uniform Building Code as set out in
Chapter 150.
   (B)   As an exception to the above, establishments which are in existence at
the time of the adoption of this chapter will be permitted to continue their
use without complying with the current adopted building code, but at any time
said establishment becomes unsafe and/or a permit is taken out to remodel,
alter or add on to any portion of said facility, the entire establishment shall
be brought into compliance with the current adopted codes and this chapter.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.03)
§ 110.078 WALL, FLOOR AND ROOF REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Any floor of an on-sale establishment shall be constructed of
elements, which are structural or non-structural in nature and covered by
material(s) which create a hard, non-absorbent surface, as required by the
Building Code adopted in §
150.025.
   (B)   Any roof of an on-sale establishment may not be occupied or utilized
as a floor. Any walls of an on-sale establishment shall be solid in nature with
the exception of areas for windows and exits. Walls shall run from grade to the
roof of the structure. Any walls shall be constructed to comply with the
requirements of the International Building Code.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.04) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.079 WINDOW REQUIREMENTS.
   For the purpose of this section, all requirements that apply to windows or
other openings in the walls of an on-sale establishment shall be those
established by the Building Code adopted in §
150.025.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.05)
§ 110.080 RESTROOM REQUIREMENTS.
   It is recognized by the City Council that during the Sturgis Motorcycle
Rally, on-sale establishments have a substantially larger need for sanitary
plumbing fixtures than during normal operations, and, in consideration of the
same, the following requirements are hereby established to determine the number
of permanent restroom fixtures and temporary restroom fixtures that will be
required of an on-sale establishment.
   (A)   The restrooms required for a licensed premises at which any alcoholic
beverage is served or consumed will be determined as follows (in no case shall
there be less than two permanent restroom fixtures for each sex).
      (1)   One restroom fixture shall be added for each sex per each
additional 50 occupants within the licensed premises. The occupancy load shall
be based upon the International Building Code wherein occupancy is determined
on the basis of one person per seven square feet within the licensed premises.
      (2)   When three or more fixtures are required for each sex, the women’s
restroom shall be required to have one additional fixture more than the men’s.
      (3)   All restroom’s hand sinks shall be installed at the ratio as
determined by the Uniform Plumbing Code.
   (B)   For determining the number of temporary restroom facilities to be
added during the period one week before the Rally and the official Rally
period, the occupancy rate for the licensed premises shall be determined as one
person per seven square feet. The same ratios as above shall then be applied,
and any additional fixtures required by the occupancy rate shall be provided in
the form of portable restroom facilities. Portable restroom facilities shall be
located upon the real property of the on-sale establishment as a condition of
meeting the requirements for the liquor license.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.06)
§ 110.081 EXIT REQUIREMENTS.
   All exits of any on-sale establishment must meet or exceed the requirements
which are laid out in the Uniform Building Code adopted by the city.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.07)
§ 110.082 OCCUPANCY REQUIREMENTS/LIMITATIONS.
   (A)   At no time shall the owner/operator exceed the occupant load, which is
issued by the Building Inspector and/or Fire Chief. Due to public safety
issues, if, at any time, the Chief of Police, the City Building Official, City
Fire Chief or their designees finds that the permitted occupant load has been
exceeded, he or she may have the sale of alcohol stopped until the occupant
load is decreased to the permitted occupant load.
   (B)   (1)   The occupant load for an on-sale establishment shall be
calculated as follows: Maximum occupant load: One occupant per each seven
square feet of the licensed premises.
      (2)   This formula will not include areas identified in the license
application such as restrooms, employee work or service areas or other areas,
which are not commonly visited by the public.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.08)
§ 110.083 INITIAL INSPECTION REQUIRED PRIOR TO SALES.
   Within 15 days after the first issuance of a license, and before the new
licensee may begin sale of alcohol, the owner shall be required to have the
establishment inspected by either the Chief of Police, the Building Inspector
or the Fire Chief.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.09)
§ 110.084 APPEAL PROCESS.
   Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Chief of Police, Building
Inspector or Fire Chief made under this subchapter shall be entitled to have
said decision reviewed by the city. If after review, said person is
unsatisfied, he or she may appeal the decision to the City Council. The process
shall be as follows.
   (A)   An aggrieved person shall first file a written request for review with
the city setting forth the basis for which he or she believes the Chief of
Police, Building Inspector or Fire Chief’s decision to be in error. The writing
shall also include the person’s name and mailing address.
   (B)   Upon receipt of a written request for review, the city shall review
his or her decision and mail a written response to the aggrieved person within
20 days.
   (C)   If the aggrieved person is not satisfied with the decision of the city
following review, he or she may file a notice of appeal with the Finance
Officer. There shall be a fee as shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee
resolution assessed for filing an appeal, which shall be paid to the Finance
Office at the time of filing the notice of appeal.
   (D)   Upon receipt of a notice of appeal, the Finance Officer shall notify
the designated city official.
   (E)   After notification of the designated city official by the Finance
Officer, the appeal shall follow the appeal provision of Chapter 37.
(Prior Code, § 3.04.10) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
§ 110.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   (1)   Any violation of the provisions of this chapter is a Class 2
misdemeanor punishable by the fee as shall be set forth in the city’s annual
fee resolution and/or incarceration in the County Jail for a period not to
exceed 30 days.
      (2)   In addition, any person holding a license under this chapter who is
found to be in violation of any provisions of this chapter shall face the
possibility of revocation or non-renewal of any license.
(Prior Code, § 3.01.03)
   (B)   Any person violating the provisions of §
110.033 is guilty of a Class 2 misdemeanor.
(Prior Code, § 3.02.19) (Ord. 2019-08, passed 11-5-2019)
