**** GENERAL PROVISIONS ****
§ 151.001 UNLAWFUL TO OBSTRUCT STREETS AND SIDEWALKS.
   (A)   No person shall encumber or obstruct any sidewalk, street, public way,
public alley or public ground within the city.
   (B)   No person shall leave standing or store any vehicle, structure or
object in any public right-of-way, street, sidewalk or on public ground which
obstructs the use of the same.
   (C)   No person shall permit merchandise to be stored upon any public right-
of-way, street, sidewalk or public ground unless authorized by City Council.
   (D)   No person shall sell any goods or merchandise upon any public street,
alley, sidewalk or public ground unless authorized by City Council.
(Prior Code, § 15.04.01) (Ord. 2003-12, passed 11-28-2003; Ord. 2005-09, passed
4-29-2005; Ord. 2007-10, passed 3-31-2007) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.002 HINDERING STREET IMPROVEMENT.
   No person shall hinder or obstruct the employees of the city in lawfully
making any improvement in any public street, road, alley, sidewalk or on any
public ground of this city, nor shall any person without proper authority tear
up, break or injure any pavement, cross walk, sidewalk or other improvement in
any public street, road sidewalk, alley or public ground in the city.
(Prior Code, § 15.04.02) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.003 NO BURNING ON STREETS.
   No person shall burn any trash, lumber, leaves, grass, straw or other
material of any kind upon, or light or have a fire of any kind upon, or allow
any gasoline or petroleum products upon, or place any dirt, trash or any other
kind of material upon any street, alley or sidewalk in the city.
(Prior Code, § 15.04.03) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.004 OBSTRUCTION OF CROSSINGS BY TRAINS.
   No person shall direct the operation, order the operation, permit the
operation or operate any railroad train in such manner as to prevent the use of
the street or roadway for the purposes of vehicular or foot travel by blocking
or otherwise preventing the movement of such traffic thereon for any period of
time longer than five consecutive minutes in duration, and if a street or
roadway is so blocked for a period of at least five minutes, it shall be left
clear for a period of at least five minutes before it is again blocked. This
section shall not apply to trains traveling continuously in the same direction
through such intersection or crossing.
(Prior Code, § 15.04.04) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.005 EASEMENTS OVER VACATED STREETS AND ALLEYS.
   Any future resolution providing for the vacation of any street or alley
shall not become effective until the owners of the streets and alleys after the
same have become vacated shall execute to the city and to the public an
easement across such streets or alleys so vacated for the installation,
operation and a maintenance of water lines, sewer lines, gas lines, electrical
lines, telephone lines and all other public utilities.
(Prior Code, § 15.04.05) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.006 EASEMENTS OVER PLATTED PROPERTY.
   Any future plat providing for the relocation of any street or alley shall
not be approved unless proper provisions and arrangements have been made for
easements for the construction, installation, operation and maintenance of any
and all public utilities then in existence or which may be erected in the
future.
(Prior Code, § 15.04.06) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.007 UNLAWFUL OBSTRUCTION AND USE.
   (A)   Generally.
      (1)   Definitions. For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
         OBSTRUCT. To render impassable without reasonable inconvenience or
hazard. No person shall be deemed to have violated this section solely because
of a gathering of persons to hear him or her speak or otherwise communicate or
solely because of being a member of the gathering.
         PUBLIC. A place to which the public or a substantial group has access,
among such places are included public streets, alleys, places, public buildings
and any places of business or amusement in which the buildings, places of
business or amusement are open to the public, or publicly owned property.
      (2)   Prohibited.
         (a)   It is unlawful for any person, without legal privilege to do so,
to obstruct any public street, alley, sidewalk, way, place or building, whether
alone or with others and who, after warning by a Code Enforcement Officer,
persists in so obstructing the same.
         (b)   It is unlawful for a person in a gathering to refuse to obey a
reasonable request or order by a police officer to move.
         (c)   It is unlawful for any person to loiter, stand or sit in or upon
any public street, alley, sidewalk or crosswalk so as to in any manner hinder
or obstruct the free passage therein or thereon of persons or vehicles passing
or attempting to pass along the same. A request or order to move addressed to a
person whose speech or other lawful behavior attracts an obstructing audience
shall be deemed reasonable if the obstruction of the public area can be
eliminated by police control of the size or location of the gathering.
         (d)   It is unlawful for any person, except as provided herein, to
place any goods, wares or merchandise for exhibition or sale upon any public
street, alley, sidewalk or any public grounds in the city, or place or cause to
be placed thereon any goods, wares or merchandise, or bottles, cans, cases,
packages, barrels or other containers, at any time for exhibition, sale or any
other purpose, or place or cause to be placed thereon, any advertising sign,
bicycle rack, popcorn stand or rack, or any other moveable property, article or
material which in any manner obstructs or interferes with the free use of such
public street, road, alley, sidewalk or public ground.
(Prior Code, § 15.06.02)
   (B)   Tree planters. For the purpose of this division (B), the placement of
tree planters and attached benches upon sidewalks by the owner of the abutting
property, or his or her agent, shall not be construed as an obstruction;
provided, that the sidewalk is approximately 15 feet in width and that there
remains a minimum of five feet between the tree planter, attached benches and
the property line, and that there remains a minimum of five feet between the
tree planter, attached benches and the back of the curb.
      (1)   The placement and design of the tree planters, attached benches and
the types of trees used shall be approved by the Building Inspector or his or
her designee.
      (2)   The owner of the abutting property or his or her agent, who places
the planters and attached benches upon the sidewalk, shall keep the trees, the
tree planters and the attached benches in a neat and satisfactory manner.
      (3)   No advertising of any kind or nature shall be permitted to be
placed upon the tree planter or attached benches.
(Prior Code, § 15.06.03)
   (C)   Sidewalk café. Notwithstanding any other provision of this code, the
City Council may by annual permit authorize businesses to operate sidewalk
cafés upon public sidewalks as hereinafter described, subject to the conditions
hereinafter set forth. A sidewalk café is an outdoor area located in the public
right-of-way which is operated and maintained by an establishment, coffeehouse,
tea shop, restaurant or bar. The sale of alcoholic beverages shall be subject
to all licensing requirements, including those set forth at SDCL § 35-4-77.1.
Sidewalk cafés may be permitted within the city for operation between the hours
of 6:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m., only if all design criteria can be met.
      (1)   Application.
         (a)   An application for a sidewalk café permit shall be filed using
CitizenServe by the proposed operator with the City Planning and Permitting
Department.
         (b)   Permit fees shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee
resolution per year regardless of what month the operator acquired the permit,
and expires December 31 of the issuance year.
         (c)   The application shall include a site plan which identifies the
location and number of tables, chairs, awnings, umbrellas, trash receptacles,
heaters, barricades and landscape features as applicable, a copy of any license
required by SDCL § 35-4-77.1 and an affidavit of compliance with that
requirement, and any other documents needed to demonstrate compliance with this
chapter. The application shall include a valid copy of all necessary licenses
and permits required by state law and county ordinance.
      (2)   Design criteria.
         (a)   Sidewalk cafés are permitted only on sidewalks with a minimum
width of five feet from the property line to the curb face. The location of the
sidewalk café must be adjacent the business operating the café and may not
extend beyond the property lines. Sidewalk cafés must maintain a clear
pedestrian path of at least five feet at all times. This pathway must be free
of any obstructions such as trees, parking meters and utilities or other
facilities such as telephone poles, fire hydrants, fire protection
appurtenances, parking meters, mailboxes or signs located in the public right-
of-way. All applicable sight triangle requirements shall be met at all times by
sidewalks. No café elements may be located within two feet of the curb face.
         (b)   All elements associated with sidewalk cafés, including, but not
limited to, tables, chairs, umbrellas, temporary barricades, heaters and
awnings must be of quality design, workmanship and materials to ensure safety
and convenience to patrons. All such elements will be reviewed as part of the
permit process.
         (c)   Elements of the sidewalk café may not be attached permanently to
the sidewalk of public right-of-way. The property owner is responsible for the
restoration of the sidewalk or public right-of-way if any damage is caused by
the sidewalk café. Physical barriers may not exceed four feet in height.
Bolting a barrier to the sidewalk is not permitted.
         (d)   Umbrellas must be designed to be secure during windy conditions.
Umbrellas must be at least seven feet above the sidewalk when open.
         (e)   Lighting for sidewalk cafés is subject to approval during the
permitting process. Such lighting shall not cause a glare to passing motorists
or pedestrians. Tabletop lighting may include candles and battery-operated
fixtures.
         (f)   Sidewalk cafés are not to broadcast loud noise that results in a
nuisance to the surrounding properties.
         (g)   Physical barricades are required if alcoholic beverages are sold
at the sidewalk café.
         (h)   No signage is permitted except for what appears on the business
and a small foldable sign placed near the sidewalk café. Any such sign shall
not contain off-premises advertising and shall not display a logo or
advertising copy other than for the sidewalk café.
      (3)   Objects for sale. Vending machines, carts or other objects for sale
are prohibited from inclusion in a sidewalk café. Nothing in this section shall
preclude the City Council from authorizing vending carts or similar uses
outside of sidewalk cafés.
      (4)   Services. All services provided to sidewalk café patrons as well as
all patron activity must occur within the designated sidewalk café area. No
alcoholic beverages may be stored or mixed in the sidewalk café.
      (5)   Supervision. The permit holder is responsible for proper
supervision of the sidewalk café to ensure the requirements of the permit are
met.
      (6)   Liability insurance. Every sidewalk café permit holder must
maintain commercial general liability insurance. The city shall be named as an
additional insured on a primary, noncontributory basis for any liability
arising directly or indirectly from the operation of a sidewalk café. A copy of
the certificate of coverage shall be provided to the city, and notice of the
termination of insurance coverage shall be provided to the City Planning and
Permitting Department. The failure to maintain or a lapse in commercial general
liability insurance while operating in the city will result in immediate
revocation of the permit issued under this section.
      (7)   Additional requirements. Permit holders must ensure that the
requirements for operation are met. These include the following.
         (a)   Patrons must wear shoes and shirts at all times.
         (b)   All sidewalk cafés must maintain at least one opening for
ingress and egress at all times. All sidewalk cafés shall abide by all
accessibility requirements of the currently adopted Building Code.
         (c)   Sidewalk cafés must adhere to size, design and other
requirements approved by the city.
      (8)   Sanitation. All areas within and surrounding a sidewalk café must
be maintained in a clean, neat and sanitary condition. All cleaning must be
performed in accordance with city regulations.
      (9)   Exceptions. An exception may be granted by the Planning and
Permitting Official to any of the provisions of the design criteria set forth
in divisions (C)(2)(a) through (C)(2)(h) above.
      (10)   Appeals. Any person or party has the right to appeal a city
planning and permitting decision according to the appeal process set in
division (D) below.
      (11)   Other laws. All permit holders shall be required to abide by all
federal, state and local laws.
      (12)   Revocation of permit.
         (a)   A sidewalk café permit may be revoked for cause, including, but
not limited to, the failure to comply with all of the standards required for
the issuance of the permit.
         (b)   A notice of intent to revoke a sidewalk café permit shall be
given in writing ten days prior to actual revocation and shall specify the area
or areas of continued failure to meet requirements and maintain conditions the
city may have imposed.
         (c)   If, during that period, proof of compliance is made by the
holder of the permit, the permit may be authorized to continue in force. If a
hearing has been requested following receipt of notice to revoke, the City
Council shall hold a public hearing on the matter and shall make a
determination whether to revoke within 30 days.
(Prior Code, § 15.06.04)
   (D)   Appeal process.
      (1)   Any person aggrieved by a decision made under this section shall be
entitled to have said decision reviewed by the city. If, after review, said
person is unsatisfied, he or she may appeal the decision to the City Council,
acting as the Board of Adjustment. The process shall be as follows.
         (a)   An aggrieved person shall first file a written request for
review with the city setting forth the basis for which he or she believes the
decision to be in error. The writing shall also include the person’s name and
mailing address.
         (b)   Upon receipt of a written request for review, the city shall
review the challenged decision and mail a written response to the aggrieved
person within 20 days.
         (c)   If the aggrieved person is not satisfied with the decision of
the city following review, he or she may file a notice of appeal with the
Finance Officer. There shall be a fee as shall be set forth in the city’s
annual fee resolution assessed for filing an appeal, which shall be paid to the
Finance Office at the time of filing the written request for review. The
Finance Officer, or appointed designee, may waive the assessed fee if the
appellant provides a reasonable basis showing hardship or lack of ability to
pay the fee.
         (d)   Upon receipt of a notice of appeal, the Finance Officer shall
notify the City Council and a public hearing on the appeal shall be held at a
regularly scheduled City Council within 30 days after the date said appeal was
filed. The Finance Office shall provide notice to the person specifying the
time, date and location of the hearing.
      (2)   The City Council may notify the aggrieved person of its decision
following the hearing; however, the Council shall issue a written decision to
the person within 20 days of the hearing. The Council may affirm or reverse the
decision.
(Prior Code, § 15.06.06)
(Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2010-09, passed 8-18-2010; Ord. 2022-04,
passed 3-7-2022) Penalty, see §
151.999
**** NAMES AND NUMBERING ****
§ 151.020 NAMES OF STREETS AND AVENUES.
   The names of the streets and avenues of the city shall be known and
designated by those names shown upon the several plats of the divisions and
subdivisions of the city within its corporate limits and as may be changed by
ordinance or resolution by the City Council, as filed and of record in the
Finance Office.
(Prior Code, § 15.02.01) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.021 SYSTEM OF NUMBERING; BASE LINES.
   The dwelling houses, business places and frontages on the streets and
avenues of the city shall be and are hereby numbered, and the respective places
of residence and of business therein shall be hereafter known and designated by
number within the limits hereinafter provided as follows.
   (A)   For the purpose of numbering said residences and places of business,
on streets and avenues, as provided herein, Main Street and Junction Avenue
shall be used as base lines.
   (B)   The residences and places of business on streets and avenues lying
north and east of said base lines shall be numbered from the base number of
1,000, and said numbers for business places and residences on said street and
avenues shall decrease at the rate of 100 for each block.
   (C)   Residences and places of business on streets and avenues lying south
and west of said base lines shall be numbered from the base number of 1,000,
and said numbers for business places and residences on said streets and avenues
shall increase at the rate of 100 for each block.
(Prior Code, § 15.02.02) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.022 ODD AND EVEN NUMBERS; HOW ARRANGED.
   (A)   Each 25-foot space measuring east, north, west and south from the base
lines shall have two numbers, one odd and one even on each street, the odd
numbers being on the right-hand sides of the streets and corresponding even
number (the next number greater) shall, where the streets run parallel to the
section lines, be directly opposite on the left-hand sides of the streets.
   (B)   For the purpose of determining the right and left-hand sides of the
streets, a person is supposed to be standing with his or her back to the base
line and facing in the direction in which the numbers increase or decrease.
   (C)   On diagonal streets, except as outlined above, the numbers shall be
directly north and south or east and west of their corresponding number.
Diagonal streets, other than those excepted above, shall take the set of
numbers corresponding to the direction most nearly assumed by the street. That
is, a street running more nearly north and south than east and west will take
the northerly set of numbers.
   (D)   On curbed streets, the set of numbers shall be used corresponding to
their average direction.
(Prior Code, § 15.02.03) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.023 SIZE AND COLOR OF NUMBERS.
   (A)   All houses or buildings fronting on any public street or avenue in the
city shall be numbered with numbers of sufficient size and of such color and
shall be located as to be easily read from the street.
   (B)   All houses shall bear the number corresponding to the space on the
street line where a line through the center of the door, at right angles to
street line intersects the centerline.
(Prior Code, § 15.02.04) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.024 CERTIFICATES OF NUMBERS.
   All certificates of correct numbers will be furnished by the Building
Inspector.
(Prior Code, § 15.02.05) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.025 TIME LIMIT FOR NUMBERING.
   All buildings which may at any time hereafter by built within the city shall
be so numbered within ten days after such buildings shall become occupied as a
dwelling or place of business.
(Prior Code, § 15.02.06) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
**** SNOW AND ICE REMOVAL ****
§ 151.040 PUBLIC NUISANCE.
   Snow and ice permitted to gather and remain upon the sidewalks of this city
is dangerous to the safety of its citizens and other using said sidewalks and
is hereby declared a public nuisance.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.01) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.041 REMOVAL BY OWNER.
   The owner or occupant of any building or any lot, parcel or plot of ground
fronting or abutting on any sidewalk shall clear said sidewalk of snow or ice
to the full width of the sidewalk within 15 hours after it has fallen or
formed. Snow removal, as required by this subchapter, prohibits any person from
placing or piling any snow within the public right-of-way of any street or
alley after the city has plowed the street or alley. In addition, it is a
violation of this subchapter for any person to place or pile snow onto the
property of another without the owner’s permission. Absentee owners are subject
to this requirement and shall make arrangements for the removal of snow and ice
accordingly.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.02) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2018-14, passed
12-28-2018) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.042 REMOVAL BY CITY; COST.
   The Finance Officer shall cause to be published in the legal section of the
official newspaper the requirements of this subchapter, which notice shall be
published for two weeks after the first meeting of the City Council in October
of each year, which publication shall constitute notification by the property
owner of the contents of this subchapter. In the event the property owner or
person so notified fails to remove the snow as required by the notice
prescribed by this section, the Building Inspector may cause the snow or ice to
be removed so that the property is in compliance with this subchapter. The
actual costs of the removal of the snow and ice, plus an administrative fee as
shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee resolution, shall be assessed upon
the lots or parcels of ground fronting or abutting said sidewalk, as provided
for in §
151.043.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.03) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.043 NOTICE; ASSESSMENT.
   (A)   The Building Inspector shall maintain an accurate account of the
amount to be assessed against each lot or parcel of ground subject to
assessment, pursuant to §
151.042. On or before May 1 of each year, the Building Inspector shall cause
this account to be delivered to the Finance Officer. The Finance Officer shall
prepare an estimate of an assessment against such lot for the removal of snow
and ice for the preceding fall and winter and shall submit the same to the City
Council for its approval on or before the second meeting in June of each year.
The Finance Officer shall prepare a notice of said meeting, which notice shall
contain the name of the property owner, the legal description of the property
to be assessed and the time and place for hearing. Notice of this meeting shall
be given by publishing a true and correct copy of this notice in the official
newspaper of the city at least one week prior to the date set for hearing, and
further, by mailing a true and correct copy of said notice to the property
owner, as shown by the records of the County Assessor, at least ten days prior
to the date set for hearing. Said mailing shall be by first-class mail, postage
prepaid.
   (B)   At the time specified in the notice, the City Council shall meet and,
if it finds the assessments correct, shall approve the same with or without
modification or amendment as it may deem proper.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.04) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.044 FILING OF ASSESSMENT.
   Within ten days after such assessment has been approved by the City Council,
the Finance Officer shall make and file a certified copy of the same in the
office of the County Treasurer and, thereupon, said assessments shall be due
and payable to the city, and shall in all respects be considered as special
assessments, as provided by statute, and the same shall draw interest at the
rate of 10% per annum from the time of said assessment until 30 days after the
approval thereof by the City Council, and thereafter at the rate of 12% per
annum.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.05) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.045 CERTIFICATION.
   If any of said assessments are not paid to the city, the Finance Officer
shall certify any such delinquent assessments to the County Auditor on or
before October 15, and the same proceeding shall be had for the collection of
said assessments as are or may hereafter be provided by statute for the
collection of special assessments.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.06) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.046 RECOVERY OF COST OF REMOVING SNOW OR ICE IN LIEU OF ASSESSMENT
AGAINST PROPERTY.
   In lieu of assessing the cost of removing snow or ice from the sidewalks
against the abutting property, the City Council may authorize the City Attorney
to recover such costs in a civil action against the owner or occupant of the
property abutting such sidewalks.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.07) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005)
§ 151.047 PARKING PROHIBITED ON DESIGNATED SNOW REMOVAL ROUTES; IMMEDIATE
TICKET AND TOW AUTHORITY.
   (A)   To facilitate prompt snow removal, it shall be unlawful for any
vehicle to be parked on any designated snow removal route within the city at
any time within 24 hours of a forecast by the National Weather Service, as
reported on the city’s website Weather Link, of an expected snowfall of at
least four inches or more within the city. The designated snow removal routes
are shown on the official map of snow removal routes available at the Finance
Office and maintained by that office, and as also shown on the city website
(www.sturgisgov.com). All designated snow removal routes shall also be marked
with signage along the designated right-of-way to identify them. Any vehicle
parked on a snow removal route within that 24-hour period and before city
employees have cleared the street curb to curb shall be subject to an immediate
citation for a parking violation until the street has been cleared curb to
curb. In addition, any vehicle tagged in violation of this subchapter may be
towed immediately after being tagged. The penalty for such violation is as set
forth in §
151.999, and the owner, in addition such penalty, shall also be required to pay
the cost of towing and removal of the vehicle to an authorized location.
   (B)   This provision shall not limit the separate authority to issue a
citation as provided for in §
72.06.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.08) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2010-13, passed
12-15-2010; Ord. 2013-18, passed 11-20-2013) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.048 DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC WORKS AUTHORITY.
   The Director of Public Works shall consult with the Chief of Police and,
consistent with the authority of SDCL § 9-30-2, the city is authorized and
empowered to determine and designate snow removal routes upon any street or
highway within the city, or any part thereof. The designation of any snow
removal route by the city shall be conspicuously posted on each block along
said route.
(Prior Code, § 15.03.09) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2010-13, passed
12-15-2010; Ord. 2013-18, passed 11-20-2013)
**** CONSTRUCTION AND MAINTENANCE OF SIDEWALKS ****
§ 151.060 BUILDING PERMIT REQUIRED.
   Before any person may construct any sidewalk in the city, he or she shall
first obtain a building permit from the Building Inspector. The application for
the building permit shall include the measurements and planned location of the
proposed sidewalk and the width of adjoining sidewalks in the same locality.
The applicant shall pay the city the sum as shall be set forth in the city’s
annual fee resolution for each application to cover the cost of processing the
application.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.01) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
§ 151.061 WIDTH AND LOCATION OF SIDEWALKS.
   The Building Inspector shall consider said application and shall determine
in said application as to the exact location and width of said sidewalk. In
determining the exact location and width of the sidewalk, the Building
Inspector shall cause as much uniformity to result as possible in the
construction of sidewalks in any one block or area. The location and width of
the sidewalk shall be included on the permit which shall be issued by the
Building Inspector to the applicant. It shall be unlawful for any sidewalk to
be built without a permit and not in conformity with the permit granted for
said sidewalk.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.02) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.062 MATERIAL.
   Any sidewalk constructed within the city shall be made of concrete unless
otherwise approved by a special request approved by the City Council.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.03) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
§ 151.063 CONSTRUCTION.
   (A)   Resolution of necessity.
      (1)   The City Council, by resolution of necessity, may deem necessary
for sidewalks to be constructed throughout the city. The resolution may require
any owner of real property who abuts or adjoins a public right-of-way, or
public property containing a highway, to construct a sidewalk in a location as
designated in the resolution. The resolution of necessity must contain the
following:
         (a)   The proposed location of the sidewalk to be constructed;
         (b)   The date by which the construction must be completed; and
         (c)   Any details, plans and specifications may be reviewed at the
Finance Office during regular business hours.
      (2)   The resolution of necessity may address multiple sidewalks within
the resolution if the above requirements along with any associated notice and
mailing requirements are satisfied for each sidewalk set forth in the
resolution.
   (B)   Notice.
      (1)   Prior to the hearing on the resolution of necessity, a notice of
hearing on the proposed resolution of necessity must be published once, not
less than ten nor more than 20 days before the hearing on the resolution of
necessity. The notice must contain the time and place of the hearing and must
state that the City Council will consider any objections to the proposed
resolution by owners of the property abutting or adjoining the sidewalk
proposed to be constructed.
      (2)   In addition to publishing the notice of hearing, the notice of
hearing must be mailed not less than nor more than 20 days before the hearing,
by first-class or certified mail, to each owner of real property abutting or
adjoining the sidewalk proposed to be constructed. The mailed notice must
contain the location of the sidewalk to be constructed, the date by which the
construction must be completed, and that the property owner is responsible for
the costs of constructing the sidewalk.
      (3)   The Finance Officer will include on said notice, upon the advice of
the Building Inspector, specifications concerning the locations of all
sidewalks to be constructed under the provisions of this section. In case said
owners are nonresidents and cannot be found, then such notice shall be given to
such nonresident owner by publication in the official paper of the municipality
once each week for two successive weeks.
      (4)   Along with the above requirements, said notice will include the
following:
         (a)   A description of the work to be done;
         (b)   The location for all sidewalks to be constructed;
         (c)   The character of all sidewalks to be constructed;
         (d)   The name of the owner of any abutting property; and
         (e)   A description of the lots or parcels of ground fronting or
abutting the sidewalk which is to be constructed.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.04) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
§ 151.064 MAINTENANCE, REPAIRS AND RECONSTRUCTION.
   (A)   The owner of property abutting or adjoining a sidewalk has the duty
and responsibility to maintain and repair the sidewalk, including all
associated costs.
   (B)   Any owner of property who fails to keep the sidewalks abutting or
adjoining the property in repair or creates or maintains a public nuisance
associated with the sidewalk, is liable to the municipality for any damage or
injury caused by neglect from the unrepaired sidewalk or nuisance. The property
owner is also responsible for any nuisance abatement costs.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.05) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.065 NOTICE OF NECESSARY MAINTENANCE, REPAIRS OR RECONSTRUCTION.
   (A)   (1)   Upon request, complaint or observation, the City Planning and
Permitting Department will inspect and make a determination whether a sidewalk
needs maintenance, repairs or reconstruction completed by the property owner.
      (2)   If the Planning and Permitting Department determines sidewalk
maintenance, repairs or reconstruction are necessary, then the Department will
send notice, by first-class or certified mail, to the property owner.
   (B)   The notice must contain the following:
      (1)   Property owner name and address (if address is different than
subject property address, then both addresses are necessary);
      (2)   The location of the sidewalk;
      (3)   A description of the current condition of the sidewalk;
      (4)   A description of the work to be done; and
      (5)   The reasonable time frame for repairs, maintenance or
reconstruction to be completed.
   (C)   The requirement for a resolution of necessity does not apply to
sidewalk maintenance, repairs or reconstruction.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.06) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
§ 151.066 INSTALLATION REQUIRED.
   (A)   A sidewalk must be installed or constructed on any vacant lot where a
new building or dwelling be constructed upon such vacant lot. Such sidewalks
must be completed at or before the time the new building or dwelling is
completed and must be constructed according to city plans and specifications.
   (B)   Provisions for a sidewalk to be omitted by the City Building Inspector
can be determined based upon the city’s curb and gutter evaluation plan.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.07) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2013-18, passed
11-20-2013; Ord. 2022-01, passed 2-14-2022)
§ 151.067 WHEN WORK NOT DONE BY OWNER.
   If such sidewalks are not constructed, maintained, reconstructed or repaired
in the manner or within the time prescribed, the City Council may, by
resolution, cause the same to be done and the cost thereof assessed against the
lots or parcels of land fronting or abutting upon the sidewalks so constructed,
maintained, reconstructed or repaired, and the cost of such work shall be
assessed and certified in the manner as provided by state law.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.08) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
§ 151.068 DEFACING SIDEWALKS.
   No person shall willfully deface, paint upon or mark upon or cause the same
to be done upon any of the sidewalks of the city.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.09) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.069 DISCHARGE OF RAINWATER.
   No person shall willfully permit rainwater discharge from any building to
move on and over any sidewalk.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.10) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.070 VARIANCES.
   The requirements under this subchapter may be modified by a variance as
described and applied for under §
156.497.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.11) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
§ 151.071 APPEAL PROCESS.
   (A)   Any person aggrieved by a decision of the Planning and Permitting
Department, or the Building Inspector made under this subchapter shall be
entitled to have said decision reviewed by the city. If, after review, said
person is unsatisfied, he or she may appeal the decision to the City Council.
   (B)   The process shall be as follows.
      (1)   An aggrieved person shall first file a written request for review
with the city setting forth the basis for which he or she believes the decision
to be in error. The writing shall also include the person’s name and mailing
address.
      (2)   Upon receipt of a written request for review, the city shall review
the challenged decision and mail a written response to the aggrieved person
within 20 days.
      (3)   If the aggrieved person is not satisfied with the decision of the
city following review, he or she may file a notice of appeal with the Finance
Officer. There shall be a fee as shall be set forth in the city’s annual fee
resolution assessed for filing an appeal, which shall be paid to the Finance
Office at the time of filing the written request for review.
      (4)   Upon receipt of a notice of appeal, the Finance Officer shall
notify the City Council and a public hearing on the appeal shall be held at a
regularly scheduled City Council within 30 days after the date said appeal was
filed. The Finance Office shall provide notice to the person specifying the
time, date and location of the hearing.
      (5)   The Council may affirm or reverse the decision of the city.
   (C)   The City Council may notify the aggrieved person of its decision
following the hearing; however, the Council shall issue a written decision to
the person within 20 days.
(Prior Code, § 15.05.12) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-01, passed
2-14-2022)
**** RIGHT-OF-WAY (ROW) MAINTENANCE ****
§ 151.085 DUTY TO MAINTAIN RIGHTS-OF-WAY.
   (A)   An owner, occupant or other person in control of real property must
maintain any and all rights-of-way which abut their property in a safe and
sanitary condition. Rights-of-way include any non-paved areas and private trees
located in the area between their property line to the adjacent curb line,
roadway/alley line if no curb and gutter are installed, and the areas on both
sides of a sidewalk or bike path. Public trees located in rights-of-way are
provided for in §§
90.080 through
90.086. All right-of-way maintenance must follow the following standards.
      (1)   Sidewalks and bike paths. All grass and weeds which sit within five
feet of either side of a sidewalk or bike path must be trimmed to a maximum
height of eight inches. All tree limbs which overhang a sidewalk or bike path
cannot fall below seven feet above the sidewalk or bike path.
      (2)   Streets and alleys. All grass and weeds must be trimmed to a
maximum height of eight inches, and all tree limbs must be trimmed at least 14
feet above any street and alley.
      (3)   Grass and weeds. All grass and weeds within the right-of-way area
described above must be maintained at a maximum height of eight inches
throughout their property and to the edge of the street or alley.
      (4)   Corners. Any bushes or shrubs within ten feet from the curb of any
corner or intersection must be kept at a maximum height of two feet.
      (5)   Fire hydrants. Property owners must remove all bushes, shrubs,
plants or trees within five feet of a fire hydrant. All grass and weeds within
five feet of a fire hydrant must be trimmed to a maximum height of eight
inches.
      (6)   Debris basin. Abutting property owners must keep debris basins
clear of any obstructions, such as fallen trees, fallen branches, construction
materials and other materials not natural to the basins, which may impede the
functionality of water running through the basin. Abutting property owners are
not required to mow or cut the grass and weeds in the debris basin, however,
they must not add any improvement or modify the debris basin in any way. This
restriction includes building any fence, structure, concrete pad or any
improvement which may affect the functionality of the debris basin. The city
currently has one debris basin located within the city limits, and extends
between Elk Road and Raccoon Road.
      (7)   General. Trim or remove all bushes, shrubs, grass, weeds, plants of
any kind or trees blocking signal lights or traffic or pedestrian signs.
   (B)   It is unlawful for a person to allow the following to accumulate on
the person’s property or in the right-of-way area described above:
      (1)   Any bush, shrub, grass, weed, plant or trees which do not meet the
above standards;
      (2)   Garbage, rubbish or brush; or
      (3)   Filth or any other unsightly, objectionable or unwholesome matter.
This provision does not include any animal carcasses in the right-of-way
because of vehicle strikes or natural reasons.
   (C)   It is a valid defense to an alleged violation of this subchapter, to
which the burden rests on the alleged violator to show with a sufficient basis,
that the weeds or grasses observed on the subject property did not reduce or
impair visibility or line of sight at, of or for right-of-way, vehicles,
cyclists or pedestrians, and that the over-height weeds or grasses observed
were located at or on one or more of the following:
      (1)   An area within or adjacent to a stream, waterway or water quality
facility;
      (2)   A landscaped area arranged and managed consistent with a plan
accepted by the city, which area includes native or adapted vegetation, where
weed control and other periodic maintenance occurs; or
      (3)   City parkland, a greenbelt, nature preserve or other publicly
maintained open space.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.01) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.086 EASEMENTS AND DRAINAGE OBSTRUCTIONS AND MODIFICATIONS.
   (A)   Property owners are responsible for maintaining any and all applicable
easements which are within their property boundaries under the specific terms
of the easements.
   (B)   Property owners must maintain and not materially obstruct, destroy,
modify or otherwise affect the function of any drainage systems which runs
across their property. If a property owner materially affects a drainage
system, the property owner is responsible for all costs to repair or
reconstruct the drainage system back to premodification condition. If more than
one property owner materially affects a drainage system which runs through all
of their properties, then all of the violating property owners are severally
and jointly liable for any and all repairs or reconstruction costs. Any
proposed drainage system modifications must be approved by the City Engineer
prior to the start of any work to ensure drainage is adequately maintained and
will not materially affect other property owners.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.02) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023)
§ 151.087 PARKING IN UNIMPROVED RIGHTS-OF-WAY.
   (A)   Parking in an unimproved right-of-way is prohibited unless the
abutting landowner, who has the responsibility of maintaining the unimproved
right-of-way, consents to parking in the abutting unimproved right-of-way.
   (B)   All parking violations occurring in unimproved rights-of-way under
this chapter are enforced by the City Police Department under the standard
parking violation procedures.
   (C)   The notice provisions under
Chapter 37 do not apply to parking violations under this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.03) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.088 ALTERNATIVE COMPLIANCE RULES.
   The city may authorize departments to develop alternative compliance rules
that permit maintenance of specified perimeters on properties defined as large
parcels, undeveloped or minimally developed, as an alternative to compliance of
the entire property under §
151.085.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.04) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023)
§ 151.089 NOTICE OF VIOLATION AND APPEALS.
   Unless excepted under this subchapter or an emergency exists, any
enforcement under this subchapter must follow the notice and hearing procedures
as outlined in
Chapter 37. Additionally, any person alleged to violate this subchapter may use
the appeal procedures as provided in
Chapter 37 to appeal the decision.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.06) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023)
§ 151.090 CITY ACTION TO CORRECT VIOLATION.
   If the responsible party fails or refuses to correct a violation of this
subchapter, the city may:
   (A)   Expend city funds to remedy the violation;
   (B)   Charge the responsible party for work performed by the city, including
all reasonable labor and abatement costs; and
   (C)   Assess the actual costs against the property.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.07) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023)
§ 151.091 EMERGENCY ABATEMENT.
   (A)   In addition to the corrective action authorized under this subchapter,
the city may take emergency action to abate a condition or circumstance that
poses an immediate danger to the public health, safety or welfare.
   (B)   The city may take immediate action to remove as an immediate danger to
a person’s health, life or safety any condition which meets the following
criteria:
      (1)   Grass or weeds which exceed 48 inches;
      (2)   Bushes, shrubs, grasses, weeds, plants or trees which obstruct the
view of a vehicle entering a public street;
      (3)   A hidden or obscured unsafe condition of land located less than 30
feet from a public street or sidewalk; or
      (4)   Is determined by the city to be an immediate danger.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.08) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023)
§ 151.092 RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER LAW.
   This subchapter is cumulative of other laws and ordinances that authorize
the city to pursue civil or criminal proceedings against an owner, occupant or
person in charge of real property, or to seek other remedies available at law.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.09) (Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12, passed
2-2-2023)
**** BRICK PROJECT ****
§ 151.105 FINDINGS.
   It is a finding of the Common Council of the city that it is in the best
interest of the citizens of the city to enter into an agreement to sell bricks
within the city for purposes of beautification; and, pursuant to SDCL § 9-46,
the city has jurisdiction to regulate its sidewalks and, therefore, this
subchapter is hereby entered to regulate the installation of engraved brick
pavers and granite blocks on the sidewalks within the city.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 1) (Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000)
§ 151.106 USE OF BRICK.
   Sidewalks within areas, designated by the Council, shall be constructed of
brick pavers or granite block. The Council, by resolution, shall designate
which areas shall have sidewalks which are to be constructed of said material,
giving regards to business needs and the amount of travel in the vicinity of
each.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 2) (Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000)
§ 151.107 SNOW AND ICE REMOVAL.
   (A)   In areas which have been designated to have sidewalks made up of
pavers or granite, the city will be responsible for the removal of snow and ice
from said sidewalks. Said property owners will be encouraged to keep the
sidewalks clean of snow and debris, however, the city will provide snow removal
for the same.
   (B)   Prior to any property owners using pressure equipment or chemicals to
remove snow and ice from their buildings, they will contact the city and advise
them of the type of equipment and chemical de-icer they plan on using. The city
must give approval of the same, before the landowner is allowed to use said
chemicals or equipment.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 3) (Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000)
§ 151.108 DEFACING AND DESTROYING BRICK PAVERS PROHIBITED.
   It shall be illegal for any person to deface or destroy a brick paver from
the sidewalk.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 4) (Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000) Penalty, see §
151.999
§ 151.109 NOTICE TO CITY.
   In the event it is necessary to remove sidewalk for purposes of utility
repair or replacement, the adjacent owner shall give the city 24 hours’ notice
so that the city may remove and replace any pavers or granite. Expenses of
labor and materials for removing said pavers or granite shall be the
responsibility of the adjacent building owner, and the city may assess costs
against the adjacent building landowner.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 5) (Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000)
§ 151.110 MAINTENANCE; FINANCE.
   Maintenance monies to repair or maintain said sidewalks shall be financed
from the City Brick Beautification Project. The city shall grant all necessary
services as set forth in the agreement between the city and Mato Paha Fund
Raisers, L.L.C., a copy of which is attached to the ordinance codified in this
subchapter and by reference made a part hereof.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 6) (Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000)
§ 151.999 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any violation of the provisions of this chapter is a Class 2
misdemeanor punishable by the maximum punishment set forth by the laws of the
state pursuant to SDCL § 22-6-2. Said punishment may also include payment of
any costs and/or restitution authorized by this chapter and/or state law.
(Prior Code, § 15.01.03)
   (B)   Any violation of §
151.007 is a Class 2 misdemeanor punishable by the maximum punishment set forth
by the laws of the state pursuant to SDCL § 22-6-2. Said punishment may also
include payment of any costs and restitution authorized by this chapter or
state law. Violations may also be subject to administrative citations pursuant
to Chapter 37.
(Prior Code, § 15.06.01)
   (C)   Any violation of §§
151.085 through
151.092 is subject to the provisions of Chapters 37, 94 and 156 and/or a Class
2 misdemeanor punishable by the maximum punishment set forth by the laws of the
state pursuant to SDCL § 22-6-2. Said punishment may also include payment of
any costs and/or restitution authorized by city code or state law, including,
but not limited to, property assessments.
(Prior Code, § 15.07.05)
   (D)   Violation of §§
151.105 through
151.110 is a Class 2 misdemeanor. In addition, the city may recover from the
offending party the cost to replace and/repair the sidewalk.
(Prior Code, Title 28, § 4)
(Ord. 2000-04, passed 5-26-2000; Ord. 2005-09, passed 4-29-2005; Ord. 2022-12,
passed 2-2-2023)
